deals.body: The Place It is a brand-new space at ION Orchard for this legendary pizzeria. I checked out the newly relocated Osteria Mozza Singapore at ION Orchard as the famous pizzeria restaurant has moved out of Hilton Singapore Orchard. Osteria Mozza Singapore is also James Beard Award-winning Chef Nancy Silverton’s only Asian outpost of the Michelin-starred restaurant concept from Los Angeles, California. The new space is much warmer, elegant and befitting of the brand when I first had it when it was in MBS eons ago. The Food Pizzas are still the highlight for us. Making its Singapore debut is Pizza alla Pala, a Roman-style pizza inspired by Rome’s vibrant street food culture. The pizza is baked in a long, paddle-shaped form (pala means “paddle” in Italian), and it features a light, airy interior and crisp crust, designed for sharing. My favourite flavour is the Funghi Misti (S$29) – taleggio, fontina, thyme, Parmigiano Reggiano. I love the crisp crust and true to its description, it is airy so it doesn’t feel too heavy. It is a tough tie between the Funghi and the Aglio e Olio (S$23) with mozzarella and fontina for me; another flavour I highly recommend, and you can

members.title: Molly Tea: 1-for-1 selected drinks

members.body:
Molly Tea has a new store in Bukit Panjang
Image credit: Molly Tea
I visit 313 Somerset often, and here’s my regular itinerary: dinner at Bari Bari Steak , a sweet treat at Yo-Chi Frozen Yoghurt , and a drink to end the day at Molly Tea . Sometimes, though, those cravings strike when I’m all the way in the West. If you’re like me, I have good news: Molly Tea just opened its third outlet at Hillion Mall , marking its first outlet in the West.
313 Somerset Food Guide: 15 Places For Chongqing Grilled Fish, Ayam Geprek And More
ICYMI: Molly Tea is a Shenzhen-born milk tea chain with over 2,000 outlets around the world. It opened two outlets in Singapore earlier this year: one at Orchard Central and the other at Raffles Place .
The menu at Hillion Mall matches the other outlets, so fans can expect their global best-seller, Premium Jasmine Milk Tea ($5.20) . The tea is brewed from Guangxi jasmine flowers through a seven-step process, then blended with milk for a light, delicate taste with a clean finish.
The Premium Jasmine Grape Milk Tea ($6.50) is a fruity variant that combines sweet grape flavours with the floral aroma of the jasmine milk tea, reminiscent of Qoo.
The Snowy Jasmine ($6.50) gets a lot of love online, and my dining companion agrees with the hype. It features the same jasmine milk tea, topped with a dollop of slightly sweet, airy jasmine whipped cream, and garnished with crushed pecans for some crunch.
My favourite, however, is the Pistachio Jasmine Coconut ($6.20) : a blend of coconut water and jasmine tea topped with a creamy, umami pistachio cheese layer that’s not too sweet. Although coconut and pistachio are pretty strong flavours on their own, they complement each other well in this drink, with a subtle jasmine fragrance coming through.
Matcha lovers should order their Velvety White Champaca ($6.90) , featuring a layer of earthy matcha cheese sitting on a base of delicate white champaca tea. Molly Tea has recently revised their matcha cheese recipe for a stronger, more umami taste that any matcha fan can appreciate.
Switch things up with the Tongmu Lapsang Milk Tea ($6.90), which uses black tea leaves from Fujian. The result is a naturally smoky drink with notes of caramel, honey, and malt.
To celebrate its opening, Molly Tea is also rolling out exclusive opening deals from 9 October to 11 October 2026 . Enjoy a 1-for-1 promotion on the six aforementioned drinks: Premium Jasmine Milk Tea, Premium Jasmine Grape Milk Tea, Pistachio Jasmine Coconut, Velvety White Champaca, Snowy Jasmine, and Tongmu Lapsang Milk Tea, limited to four redemptions per order.
Additionally, the first 50 customers will receive an exclusive Insulated Tumbler dressed in Molly Tea’s signature pink. Customers 51 to 150 can enjoy a Purple Grape Scented Candle, while customers 151 to 250 get a Singapore-exclusive Glitter Fridge Magnet .
If you missed the chance to be one of the first few customers, you can still get a free Pink Iconic Bag when you follow @mollytea.sg on Instagram or TikTok.
There’s also a Flower Market Pop-Up running from 9 October to 22 October 2026 , complete with an aesthetic flower wall photo spot that’s perfect for the ‘gram.
You can even take home a complimentary flower if you present your receipt and share a photo taken at the flower wall on social media, while stocks last.
Molly Tea is located in Hillion Mall, a two-minute walk from Bukit Panjang MRT Station .
For more eats in the locale to pair with your Molly Tea, check out our guide to the best food in Bukit Panjang . Alternatively, if you’re looking for another drink to quench your thirst, read our AiFOKATO feature , a Hanok-inspired cafe serving the viral gelato affogato.
Address: 17 Petir Road, #B1-42/43, Hillion Mall, Singapore 678278
Opening hours: Daily 10am to 10pm
Website
Molly Tea is not halal-certified.

Doughnut lovers, good news! I’m donut? , the Japanese doughnut brand that has drawn long queues and a cult following, is coming to Singapore this December .
Credit: I’m donut?
This will be I’m donut?’s Singaporean debut, and it will open its first store at ION Orchard’s Basement 2 . For those who have been waiting for the popular doughnut brand’s arrival, they are probably looking forward to the signature nama doughnuts they have become so beloved for.
Credit: I’m donut?
These doughnuts, which have made waves across social media, are known for their “pillowy”, light, fluffy, and extra-soft texture. This is the result of founder Ryouta Hirako’s reimagination of what a doughnut could be.
Complementing the airy texture of the doughnuts are a variety of creamy fillings and delicate toppings, which bring satisfaction and surprise with every bite. You will experience a springy delight that melts in your mouth, no matter which flavour you go for.
Credit: CapitaLand
I’m donut? first opened its doors and built a fanbase in Japan in 2022. In just 4 years, it has brought its nama goodness to cities like New York, Taipei, and Seoul. Now, it’s finally coming to our Little Red Dot, ready to spread its sweet joy to more doughnut fans internationally.
For more information on the Singapore store’s exact opening date, stay tuned to their Instagram page .

To be announced

Donut lovers, here’s something exciting to look forward to. I’m donut?, the hugely popular Japanese nama donut brand, is coming to Singapore.
Founded by Japanese chef Ryouta Hirako, I’m donut? has become a sensation for its signature nama donuts, which are incredibly soft, light and almost melt-in-your-mouth. Unlike a typical donut, its original brioche-style dough incorporates pumpkin and undergoes a long, low-temperature fermentation before being fried at high heat, resulting in its distinctive fluffy and airy texture.
The brand started in Japan and has since expanded overseas to cities including New York, Taipei and Seoul. Most recently, it made its Southeast Asian debut at The Exchange TRX in Kuala Lumpur on 12 September 2026, where more than 200 people reportedly queued before the store even opened.
Besides the signature I’m donut? Original, the brand is also known for flavours such as custard cream, matcha, cacao and pistachio, with different cities receiving their own exclusive creations.
Photos credit: I’m Donut?
Details on the Singapore location and opening date have yet to be officially confirmed, but judging from the queues at its other overseas openings, we can probably expect plenty of excitement when I’m donut? finally arrives in Singapore.

members.body:
I’m Donut? is opening in Singapore
Image credit: The New Yorker
Frequent Japan visitors like me are probably familiar with I’m Donut , a Japanese doughnut chain that built a cult following for their fluffy nama doughnuts and has over 10 outlets in Japan. After announcing the launch of their first Malaysian outlet in KL, I’m Donut has just teased the opening of their first store in Singapore.
Japan’s Viral I’m Donut To Open First Malaysia Outlet In KL On 12 Sep
Image credit: @i.m.donut
In December 2026 , the chain will debut in Singapore at ION Orchard , Basement 2, bringing its signature nama donuts to local fans for the first time.
Image credit: I’m Donut
In case you don’t know, I’m Donut uses a brioche dough that’s enriched with pumpkin and fermented at low temperatures before it’s fried quickly at high heat. The doughnuts are then topped with a variety of creams and toppings made fresh in-house. The result is a light, airy, and clean-tasting doughnut said to melt in your mouth.
Image credit: I’m Donut
The menu for Singapore’s outlet isn’t out yet, but you can probably expect to see their best-selling I’m Donut? Original (price TBD) , a powdered sugar doughnut made with the aforementioned brioche dough. Their Custard Cream (price TBD) is another popular variant, with Kyushu cream whipped into a smooth Diplomat cream and generously piped inside. Matcha lovers can also look forward to their popular I’m Donut? Matcha (price TBD) , featuring dough that’s said to have been kneaded and fully coated with Yame matcha from Fukuoka.
Image credit: Keisuke Tanigawa via Time Out
Every item is handmade in-house, from the dough to the fillings and toppings.
Currently, that’s all the details we have. However, we’ll be on the lookout for more updates.
In the meantime, check out Yamamoto Hamburg , another Japanese chain outlet that has opened its doors in Singapore, specialising in Japanese hamburg. If you’re looking for Japanese pastries instead, our guide to the best Japanese cafes in Singapore has you covered.
Address: 2 Orchard Turn, #B2-19, ION Orchard, Singapore 238801
Opening hours: TBD
Website
I’m Donut is not halal-certified.

members.body:
Donut fans in Singapore , here’s one to add to your watchlist. I’m Donut?, the Japanese brand known for its fluffy, melt-in-the-mouth creations, is officially opening in Singapore this December at Ion Orchard! While the menu and prices haven’t been announced yet, there’s plenty to know about the brand before it lands here.
I’m Donut? Singapore: Details at a glance
Best for: Donut lovers and fans of Japanese-style pastries
When: Officially opening in December 2026
How much: To be confirmed
Address: I’m Donut? , B2-19, Ion Orchard, 2 Orchard Turn, Singapore 238801
What is I’m Donut?
Photography: I’m Donut? via Instagram
Founded by chef Ryouta Hirako, I’m Donut? was born out of experiments with the dough used in his bakery. The name is a playful nod to the idea that a donut doesn’t have to be what you expect.
Unlike the denser, chewier rings you might be familiar with, these Japanese-style donuts are known for their soft, airy texture. I’m Donut?’s first outlet opened in Tokyo’s Nakameguro neighbourhood, introducing diners to its signature nama donuts.
Since then, the Japanese brand has expanded internationally, with outlets in cities including New York, Taipei, Seoul and Kuala Lumpur.
What to expect at I’m Donut? Singapore
Photography: I’m Donut? via Instagram
The menu is still under wraps, so you’ll have to wait a little longer to see which flavours make the cut. But the brand’s overseas offerings give us a few ideas of what to look out for.
The original nama donut is a natural starting point for anyone keen to try the signature treat in its simplest form. Matcha and chocolate varieties offer more familiar flavour options, while cream-filled versions such as custard and matcha cream are worth keeping an eye out for. I’m Donut? also serves other styles, including glazed and chocolate-coated donuts.
There’s room for a little regional inspiration, too The KL outlet has featured creations inspired by familiar favourites, including Milo, pandan and banana fritter caramel. Whether Singapore will get its own exclusive flavours remains to be seen. But we’re keeping our fingers crossed! Imagine a durian nama donut or one inspired by ondeh-ondeh…
Psst: follow I’m Donut?’s official Instagram account to keep tabs on its opening in Singapore!
Frequently Asked Questions
When and where is I'm Donut? opening in Singapore?
The Japanese donut shop is opening at Ion Orchard this December.
Is this a temporary pop-up or a permanent flagship store?
This is a permanent standalone store, marking the brand's first official brick-and-mortar outlet in Singapore following expansions to New York, Taipei, Seoul and Kuala Lumpur.
What is a nama donut?
Despite the name nama (which means "raw" in Japanese), the dough is fully cooked! It refers to the cloud-like, ultra-moist and springy texture that melts softly in your mouth.
What’s the secret behind the dough?
The unique texture comes from a specialised dough process: brioche base enriched with roasted pumpkin, low-temperature fermentation and handmade creams.
What signature flavours can we expect at the Singapore store?
While the exact local launch menu is under wraps, core global favourites include the original, custard cream, matcha and pistachio & chocolate.
Will there be Singapore-exclusive flavours?
Yes. The Singapore team is expected to unveil local-exclusive flavour collaborations closer to launch.

members.body: IKEA Singapore is giving every child aged 12 and under a free oat vanilla ice cream cone on Children's Day, Friday 2 October 2026, at the Swedish Bistro in Alexandra, Tampines and Jurong. IKEA's own bistro page sets the rules: one day only, while stocks last, the child has to be there to claim it, one cone per child, and staff may ask for proof of age such as a student concession card. It is not a big saving, since the cone usually costs 50 cents, but it needs no purchase and no IKEA Family membership. Two things decide where you go. Jurong's bistro opens earliest, at 10am, and at Tampines the Level 1 halal bistro's menu does not list the oat cone, so use the Level 3 bistro there.

members.body: The Place Located at Raffles City is a new tonkatsu and udon restaurant from Seoul. OJEJE (오제제) just opened its first international foray in Singapore at the basement of Raffles City, where the brand is founded in 2020 by Chef-Owner Kim Ji-hoon. Hailing from Jeju Island, OJEJE operates six directly managed restaurants in Seoul, with Singapore marking the beginning of its first global journey. The Food The udon noodles are made fresh in-house, and each cut of the pork is assessed individually during the wet-aging process before being fried. OJEJE’s signatures include its Pork Loin Katsu, Premium Matcha Zaru Udon, alongside the brand’s distinctive Kadaif Prawn and other favourites. I had their Pork Loin Katsu + Kadaif Prawn Set (S$38) where the air-flown pork loin is wet-aged for tenderness and trimmed to balance lean meat with natural fat. There are a few ways to enjoy the tonkatsu – as is, with a dipping sauce or with a pinch of Himalayan salt. It is also served with Black Tiger Prawns wrapped in fine kadaif pastry paired with white truffle sauce. New Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella at BreadTalk
Chocolate is one thing I can’t live without, so you can imagine how happy I was when I found out about Nutella ’s collaboration with BreadTalk . They’re teaming up for the new Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella , available for a limited time only, at participating BreadTalk outlets.
Even better, you can score one for free. From 1 Oct to 11 Nov 2026 , simply spend $10 on Nutella Spreads at participating retailers to redeem a free Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella . And since the promo covers both major supermarkets and online grocery platforms, it’s easy enough to qualify during your next grocery run. Here’s all you need to know:
BreadTalk’s Hazel Cacao Bun, paired perfectly with Nutella
This collab takes one of BreadTalk’s most famous buns, the Hazel Cacao bun, and gives it a Nutella-filled makeover. The new Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella (from $2.50) features soft natural chocolate yeast dough topped with a crunchy bolo crumble, bringing together hazelnut and chocolate in one very snackable bun.
Sink your teeth into it and you’ll find Nutella’s smooth, silky spread tucked inside, so you get that familiar hazelnut-cocoa flavour with every bite. Plus, there’s a little extra texture from the crumble on top.
It’s a no-brainer, if you ask us. But do note that the Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella is available for a limited time only at participating BreadTalk outlets. Read on for a full list of outlets where you’ll be able to find it, and the simple redemption mechanics.
The promotion is available across a pretty wide range of retailers too, including FairPrice, Giant, Cold Storage, Sheng Siong, Prime, RedMart, pandamart, Phoon Huat, and Bake With Yen. That means you can qualify whether you’re doing your usual supermarket run in the neighbourhood or restocking your pantry online from the sofa.
Once you’ve spent at least $10 on Nutella Spreads at one of the participating retailers, hang on to your receipt – you’ll need it for the next step.
Head to the Nutella promotion website and upload your receipt for verification. Once it has been approved, you’ll receive a voucher that can be used to redeem one free Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella at participating BreadTalk outlets.
The promotion runs from 1 Oct to 11 Nov 2026 , while the redemption period stretches a little longer, from 1 Oct to 30 Nov 2026 . So even if you make your Nutella purchase closer to the end of the promotion, you’ll still have some extra time to claim your bun.
Do note that the Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella is a limited-time item, so it’s probably best not to leave your redemption till the very last minute. Once your voucher is sorted, all that’s left to do is head down to a participating BreadTalk outlet and collect your chocolatey freebie. Here’s the full list of participating outlets:
AMK Hub, Bedok Mall, Causeway Point, Chinatown Point, Clementi Mall, Compass One, Eastpoint Mall, Great World, Hougang Mall, Breadtalk IHQ, ION LINK, Junction 8, Jurong Point, Marina Bay Sands, NEX, Northpoint City, Novena Square, One Holland Village, Parkway Parade, Punggol Coast Mall, Plaza Singapura, 313@Somerset, Sun Plaza, Tampines Mall, Tiong Bahru Plaza, Toa Payoh HDB Hub, VivoCity, Waterway Point, Westgate, West Mall, Wheelock Place.
Get a free BreadTalk Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella this October
Nutella’s smooth, creamy texture makes it an easy addition to all sorts of breakfast combinations. Spread it over toast, pair it with different breads, or work it into your usual breakfast rotation. It’s a must-have in every pantry.
And now, Nutella and BreadTalk’s first-ever collab is an easy win, especially since Nutella is already a pantry staple at home. Just spend $10 on Nutella Spreads at a participating retailer, upload your receipt, and redeem a free Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella while the promotion is still running.
Redeem a free Hazel Cacao Bun with Nutella on Nutella’s website
This post was brought to you by Nutella.

links.title: KFC Gen B Buffet: Unlimited O.R. Tenders and Chicken Bites for $25.95 at KFC *SCAPE, Fri 16 Oct 2026
KFC Has $25.95 One-Day Buffet At SCAPE: Unlimited Tenders, Bites And Sauces

members.body:
KFC Gen B Buffet to take place at SCAPE on 16 October
Image credit: KFC
Big eaters, clear your Friday evening on 16 October 2026 . KFC is throwing a one-day-only Gen B Buffet at its *SCAPE outlet, where $25.95 per person gets you 90 minutes of unlimited boneless chicken and a free-flow sauce bar.
This isn’t the first time the fast food chain has gone all-you-can-eat. A couple of years back, it ran an Unlimited Chicken Feast across five outlets. This time, the spread is entirely boneless. It’s part of KFC’s new Gen B campaign, which targets diners who want their fried chicken with zero bone-picking involved.
At the buffet, you can go back for as many Original Recipe (O.R.) Tenders and Chicken Bites as you can handle. Whipped Potato and fountain drinks are also free-flow. The tenders are strips of chicken tenderloin breaded in KFC’s Original Recipe seasoning. The Chicken Bites are chunks of thigh meat, not the processed nugget kind.
Image credit: KFC
The sauce bar is where things get interesting. Alongside O.R. Gravy , there are five dips to rotate through: Flaming Hot , Cheezy Onion , Shhh Secret Grill , and two newcomers. Chipotle Honey Mustard combines sweet honey and sharp mustard, with chipotle adding a mild, smoky kick. Seoul Spicy stirs Korean gochujang into a garlic aioli for something sweeter and punchier.
There are only two sessions: 5pm to 6.30pm and 7 pm to 8.30pm . Each ticket covers one person for a single 90-minute slot, and you’ll get 10% off when you book for two people or more. Tickets are sold through KFC’s online merch store .
If you’re the competitive sort, there’s also The Zermaxx Challenge. It’s named after competitive eater Zermatt Neo, who once cleared 100 KFC tenders in 40 minutes. Buffet-goers can opt in and try to eat as many O.R. Tenders as possible in one go. You’ll need at least 30 to qualify, and the count is capped at 100. The person who eats the most in the fastest time takes home $5 per tender. That works out to $150 for the bare minimum and $500 if you match Zermatt’s record!
Image credit: KFC
If you can’t make it on the day, the two new sauces have been available since 30 September at all KFC outlets except the Singapore Zoo branch. They’re also on KFC Delivery, GrabFood, and foodpanda, while stocks last. The easiest way to try both is the Double Dip Platter Meal ($8.95) . It comes with two O.R. Tenders, four Hot & Crispy Bites, medium fries, a Coke Zero Sugar, and a dip of each.
*SCAPE is near Somerset MRT Station , so you can walk off the tenders along Orchard Road afterwards. For more all-you-can-eat spreads, check out our best hotel buffets in Singapore guide .
Address: 2 Orchard Link, #02-18, *SCAPE, Singapore 237978
Buffet hours: 16 October 2026, 5pm to 6.30pm and 7pm to 8.30pm
Website
KFC is halal-certified.

deals.body:
Maison Yoshoku is open at Raffles City with hitsumabushi-style lunch sets, yoshoku à la carte plates and a dessert omakase bar under one roof at 252 North Bridge Road, #03-43.
Maison Yoshoku at Raffles City #03-43. Photo: Maison Yoshoku
Maison Yoshoku frames the room as Western comfort with Japanese craft. CapitaLand’s Raffles City directory carries the same unit and treats the dessert omakase bar as Singapore’s first of its kind.
Hours
The restaurant is open daily. Lunch runs from 11.30am to 3pm, with last order at 2.30pm. The dessert bar is open from 3pm to 10pm, with the last dessert omakase order at 9pm. Dinner service is 5.30pm to 10pm, with last order at 9.30pm.
Hitsumabushi-style seabass meuniere from Maison Yoshoku’s lunch offer. Photo: Maison Yoshoku
Three strands on one floor
The site splits the offer into Hitsumabushi Lunch, Yoshoku À La Carte and Dessert Omakase. Lunch reworks grilled protein over rice in the hitsumabushi format, including fish such as seabass meuniere. Dinner leans on Japanese-Western comfort plates such as grilled spring chicken.
Hitsumabushi here is eaten in four stages: first with salt, then with demi-glace, then with pickles, and finally with warm dashi poured over as an ochazuke-style finish. Lunch mains run from orange and rosemary chicken at $30 to black garlic wagyu at $40, with farm seabass meunière, garlic and shiso prawn and sansho unagi kabayaki at $35. The Maison Journey lunch set is $68 nett with a starter, hitsumabushi, chawanmushi, dessert and coffee or tea.
The dessert bar
The dessert omakase is a seven-course menu called The Seven Memories. It opens with green apple, lemongrass and kaffir lime, moves through kinako with kuromitsu and a nitrogen-frozen yuzu meringue with yuzu kosho sorbet, and closes with red miso and shiso.
Booking
Reservations run through the Oddle link on the restaurant’s site. Raffles City sits above City Hall MRT.

deals.body: KFC Singapore's 2 Chicken Meals for $10 returns for three days, Monday 21 to Wednesday 23 September 2026. The $10 buys two meals of 2 pieces of chicken each, so 4 pieces in total, plus 2 regular Whipped Potatoes and 2 regular Coca-Colas. KFC's poster prints U.P. $31.70, which is exactly what those eight items cost à la carte on its own menu, not what two meals cost. KFC's regular 2 pcs Chicken Meal is $9.95 and already comes with two sides and a drink, so two of them are $19.90. Against that, the deal saves $9.90 (about half) and hands you two fewer sides. It is still a genuine $5 meal. The conditions sit in the poster's small print: over-the-counter and self-ordering kiosk only (no app, website or delivery), dine-in or takeaway, a maximum of 2 sets per transaction, Original Recipe or Hot & Crispy with no choice of parts, sides fixed, while stocks last, and not at Punggol Oasis Terrace, Jurong Spring Express, Jewel, Sentosa, Singapore Poly or the Zoo.

deals.body: Soup Restaurant is marking its 35th birthday with 35% off its Signature Samsui Ginger Chicken for five weekdays, Monday 14 to Friday 18 September 2026, dine-in only. The website headline just says "35% off our Signature Samsui Ginger Chicken", but the campaign poster's fine print narrows it: small portion only, limited to one per table per bill, not valid with any other promotion, while stocks last. The small plate is $23.90++ on the brand's own menus, so it comes to about $15.54++, or roughly $18.63 nett against $28.66, a saving of about $10. Because it cannot be combined, the Early Bird discount (20% to 35% off the whole order at off-peak hours) will often save more, so the birthday deal works best at peak lunch and dinner, and at Jewel and Paragon, where Early Bird does not run. Hougang Mall is closed for renovation until the end of September.

deals.body: Buy 1 Get 1 Free The Soup Expert, the Chinese "soup in a pot" chain at Suntec City, is running Buy 1 Get 1 Free on its new sizzling claypots until 31 October 2026. Every $40 nett on one bill unlocks one free claypot, capped at two per bill, so a table spending $80 nett gets two. The claypots include Glazed Beef ($28.90), Yellow Chilli Fish Slices ($21.90) and Ginger Chicken ($19.90), all before service charge and GST. Here's how the spend threshold works, what one claypot alone leaves you short of, and what the brand's post doesn't spell out.

The usual Medium Tub comes with fewer toppings, so Quad Pop is built for the mix-everything crowd: fruit, crunch, sauces, all four in one tub. The fine print worth knowing: it applies to Medium Tub purchases only, additional toppings beyond the four are chargeable, it cannot stack with other promotions or vouchers, and it is in-store only, not on delivery platforms.

deals.body: $8.80 student meal COLLIN'S has put a student meal on its promotions page: eight dishes at $8.80, with a free Wild Mushroom Soup, Coke or Sprite, all day from Monday to Sunday. Its own T&C set the limits. It is dine-in only and only at five of its 11 restaurants (Northpoint City, Marina Square, VivoCity, The Woodleigh Mall and Tampines 1), so Westgate, Paya Lebar Quarter, NEX, Sengkang Grand Mall, Shaw Plaza and Mandai Wildlife West are out. Prices carry 10% service charge and GST, which makes the $8.80 about $10.55 at the till, and the Classic Mixed Grill and COLLIN'S Cheeseburger cost $5 more (about $16.55). A float costs $3 extra. It cannot be combined with other promotions, membership privileges or vouchers, and Collin's has published no end date, only "limited time offer".

deals.body: The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf Singapore has put its 6-inch Japanese Roasted Black Sesame Yuzu Cake on a flash deal: $30 for the whole cake instead of $60, ordered between Monday 21 September and Sunday 4 October 2026 on coffeebean.com.sg or at any outlet. Two things on Coffee Bean's own pages change the maths. First, this is a pre-order: the cakes are only collected from 15 October to 8 November 2026, with limited slots per day and no changes to the date or outlet once the order is confirmed. Second, the cake FAQ charges a flat $20 to deliver any order under $300, so a delivered cake costs $50 and two-thirds of the saving goes to the courier. Collect it from an outlet and the full $30 off is yours. A 9-piece Mini Blueberry Muffins party pack can be added for $10, and the deal does not stack with any other offer.

deals.body: $2 add-on Korean tofu-gelato brand Tofu G has a self-serve toppings bar at its two newest outlets, Suntec City #B1-K5 and Waterway Point #01-53. Add $2 to any gelato and take as much as fits in the cup from 12 toppings: injeolmi, joripong, yakgwa, puffed rice, tempeh chips, five kinds of nuts, dried cranberries and marshmallow. With an $8 scoop, a fully loaded cup comes to $10. No end date has been published, and the bar is not at Tofu G's four other outlets.

deals.body: Kenangan Coffee Singapore's payday Buy 1, Free 1 is back, and it runs to Thursday 24 September 2026. Buy one Regular coffee in the Kenangan Coffee app and a second Regular of the same flavour is free. deals.body: $3++ (U.P. $8.80), WEEKDAYS ONLY Jack's Place has a kids' menu at $3++ against a usual price of $8.80, and its own poster carries two conditions that every deal listing has dropped. The first is that the $3++ is an add-on, not a standalone: it applies only when an adult at the table orders an a la carte or promotional main course, and the restaurant's own terms then rule out the Set Lunch, which is the cheapest adult main on the menu. The second is the calendar. This is a weekday deal, Monday to Friday all day, which for most of the year is the one window when school-going children cannot use it. The 5 to 13 September school holidays are the exception, and they hand families five qualifying weekdays from Monday 7 to Friday 11 September. Three dishes sit at $3++ (Spaghetti Beef Bolognese, Chicken Nuggets & Fries, Kids' Fish & Chips), every kids' meal comes with apple juice and a single scoop of ice cream, and a $5++ tier (U.P. $10.80) buys a Minute Striploin Steak with Chicken Chipolata Sausages. After the 10% service charge and 9% GST the $3++ plate lands at about $3.60 against $10.55, so roughly $6.95 a child a visit. The deal is dine-in only, for children under 10, at the 12 outlets on the brand's own locations page, and eves of and public holidays are out, along with special occasions: the poster names Children's Day, which falls on Friday 2 October 2026.

deals.body: Hokkaido Baked Cheese Tart posted its 10th-anniversary offer on its own Facebook page on Tuesday afternoon, 1 September 2026: buy one Original Cheese Tart and get one free, from 12pm onwards, while stocks last. The catch is in the scheduling rather than the discount. The brand's poster splits the promotion across two days and pairs the outlets, so Wednesday 2 September runs at Jurong Point #B1-K2 and Parkway Parade #01-23B only, and Thursday 3 September moves to Changi Airport Terminal 3 #B2-11 and Bugis Junction #B1-K6 only. Turn up at the right shop on the wrong day and there is no offer. Causeway Point, the fifth of the five Singapore outlets the brand lists on its own page, is not in the promotion at all. The offer covers the Original Cheese Tart only, not the salted egg or durian versions, and the brand publishes no price list of its own, so the value of the free tart is whatever that outlet's counter charges. The Changi Airport shop is landside in the public basement, so you do not need a boarding pass to use it there.

deals.body: $106.82 (U.P. $160.88) Crystal Jade Hong Kong Kitchen is running a Family Roast Bundle for five to six people to 31 December 2026: a Lucky 5 Crispy Chicken, a slab of crispy pork belly (about 360g) and your choice of Hong Kong egg noodle with shredded char siew or Yang Zhou fried rice. Nearly every writeup prices it at $98 against a $147.60 usual price, but Crystal Jade's own e-store shows $106.82 for Jadeite members and $160.88 usual, and states that every price listed includes 9% GST. Those are the same numbers with tax added, so $106.82 is what you actually pay, and the saving is $54.06, about 34% off. The catches are real: the discount is for Jadeite members only (free to join in the Crystal Jade SG app), you must pre-order at least three working days ahead through the e-store or in store, there is no delivery at all, and Tampines One is the one Hong Kong Kitchen outlet left out.

The free cup is always the cheapest in the order, so two Yoghurt lattes plus one Strawberry cost exactly what three Yoghurt lattes do. The in-app voucher has to be applied before you pay, confirmed orders cannot be refunded, large cups are $1 more, and deal sites reading the voucher terms report that Burlington Square and the airport outlet are left out.

deals.body: 30% off Dian Xiao Er's promotions page is carrying three separate weekday discounts at once, and they pay out very differently. The Happy Hour poster is the simple one: 30% off, Monday to Friday 2.30pm to 4.29pm, valid on dine-in and takeaway, with no outlet list attached. The Early Bird poster looks bigger but is split in two: 30% off is exclusive to City Square Mall, Downtown East, Great World, Lot One and Parkway Parade, and the other 14 Singapore outlets get 20%, in narrower windows (11am to 12pm and 4.30pm to 6pm on weekdays, 15% at every outlet on weekends) and with a 60-minute dining limit. Sitting across both is the Set Lunch for 2 at $36.80++ for members and $38.80++ otherwise, which is explicitly not valid with other promotions, so you have to choose. We priced the set's own dish list against Dian Xiao Er's published menu, and the answer is not the one the headline discount suggests: the three cheapest picks come to exactly $38.80 a la carte, so 30% off beats the set by $11.64, but the three priciest come to $52.20 and the gap narrows to $2.26, and once you add back the dessert and two bowls of rice that the set includes and the discount excludes, the set is ahead from the middle of the range upward. VivoCity is the outlier, where the same set runs only from 2.30pm to 4.29pm.

deals.body: noci bakehouse is the Korean-style bakery cafe at Suntec City Tower 3 that keeps going viral for its salt bread, and there is a backstory most posts miss: it is run by Goldmoon, the group behind Korean pasta bar Noci, and it sits in the exact unit where Goldmoon hosted the queue-heavy pop-up of Ulsan's Yoon Yeon Dang bakery last year. The salt bread starts at $4, with a Crispy version at $5.50 and a Castella Milk Cream one at $5.90, alongside spring onion cream cheese bagels ($7), the $2.50 Viral Butter Tteok and an all-day brunch menu from $11.50++. Over 25 bakes rotate daily, 8.30am to 8.30pm. Not halal-certified.

deals.body: Elijah Pies, the homegrown pie brand that began in 2014 with a single Nutella pie, opens its second dine-in cafe and biggest space yet at 72 Joo Chiat Place on Saturday 12 September 2026. It is a heritage shophouse with 60 seats, a private room and a pet-friendly outdoor corner, and the menu that comes with it is the real news: Elijah's Souffle Pie at S$18 is dine-in only and cannot be delivered, a Kaya Toffee Pie joins the regular menu at S$9, and a new six-inch "Pizza Pie" series on a 27-layer croissant crust runs S$22 to S$24. Dogs get a S$9 pie by Petissier and a free cookie, young children get free babyccinos and cheese crisps. The catch: opening hours have not been published anywhere. As of 8 September the brand's own website has no Joo Chiat page at all, and it contradicts itself on the Tanjong Pagar hours, so call before you plan a weeknight visit there.

deals.body: Sushidan, the Tokyo sushi-ya attached to MICHELIN-starred Chef Hiroyuki Sato of Ginza's Hakkoku, opens its second Singapore outlet at Parkway Parade on Friday 5 September 2026, and it lands on the first Friday of the September school holidays. The draw is the price floor: sushi from $1.99++ a piece, sashimi from $2.99++, hand rolls from $3.99++, and omakase-style sets from $19.90++, which is $23.86 once the 10% service charge and 9% GST are on. Riding with the opening is a single dated offer, and it is the biggest number on the page: 30g of premium Hokkaido nama uni served with toasted seaweed, added to any omakase course for $18.80++ instead of $38.80++, from 5 to 30 September 2026. That is $20 off the add-on, a little over half price, and it is exclusive to the Parkway Parade outlet, so the Raffles City flagship does not honour it. Two things decide whether the trip is worth it. The uni is while stocks last and the variety can rotate with the season, and the new outlet seats about 35, roughly half of Raffles City, which is a small room to absorb an opening weekend in a school holiday week.

deals.body: Giant's weekly Super Savings flyer runs from Thursday 24 to Wednesday 30 September 2026, and its loudest line is China Premium Shine Muscat 650g at 2 for $5.95, printed as 72% off a usual $21.90. The price is real and it is the cheapest pair of these grapes we found, but the discount is not: FairPrice Online sells the same China Premium Shine Muscat 650g at $5.95 a box as its regular price and $4.95 on offer to 1 October, so a pair costs $9.90 there and Giant saves you $3.95, not $15.95. The grapes are also in the "4 Days Price Off" block, which ends on Sunday 27 September. The better value is in the freezer: Ben & Jerry's at any 3 for $25 is $8.33 a tub, while FairPrice charges $24.90 for two and $15.18 for a single. Cadbury 180g blocks at any 2 for $10 ($15 at FairPrice), Carlsberg 12 x 320ml at $24.50 and Wolf Blass Eaglehawk at $14.90 also come out ahead. Four Buy 1 Get 1 Free lines only pay if you take both, and 42 of the 68 offers need two or more units.

deals.body: McDonald's Singapore is running a Children's Day campaign called My McDonald's, My Way from 24 September to 7 October 2026. Ask the counter for a Promise Bookmark, let your child pick how the family will celebrate, sign it together and show it to staff for a free Vanilla Cone. The second part is Build My Meal, where kids mix and match their own three-item meal, desserts included, ordered at the self-ordering kiosk or through Mobile Order in the McDonald's app. The catches: McDonald's has not published a price for Build My Meal, so check the kiosk before you commit, and six restaurants (NTU, Temasek Polytechnic and four Caltex and Shell petrol-station outlets) do not have the bookmark.

deals.body: Old Chang Kee put its Mid-Autumn puff back on the counter on Tuesday 1 September, and this year it has mochi in it. The Salted Egg Taro Mochi'O (咸蛋芋泥麻薯角) is a 福-stamped puff filled with taro paste, a whole salted egg yolk and a stretch of mochi, and the brand's own promotions page lists it at all Old Chang Kee outlets from 1 to 30 September 2026, or while stocks last. The counter price is $3.80 for one and $6.80 for two, which works out at $3.40 a piece. That price is worth reading against Old Chang Kee's own back catalogue: last year's Mid-Autumn puff, the Salted Egg Yam'O, carried the same Chinese name and the same 福 stamp at $3.60 a piece, so the single has gone up $0.20 while the 2-for rate actually lands $0.20 under it. The Red Bean Mochi'O that ran from 6 May to 6 June this year was $2.60. Mid-Autumn Festival falls on Friday 25 September 2026, which leaves a five-day tail on the promotion, and the brand's line for this item names outlets only, unlike its other current items which say outlets and delivery platforms.

deals.body: From $3.20++ Genki Sushi's Crayon Shinchan collaboration runs from 24 September to 8 November 2026, with 14 limited-time dishes led by a Signature Cheesy Ebi Fry Taco at $3.20, a Shinchan Cheeky Chicken Katsu Rice at $8.90, a Miso Butter Corn Ramen at $8.60 and an Azuki Matcha Jelly Soft Serve at $6.90. Every $50 spent earns a gachapon-style spin for Genki vouchers, a Shinchan cup holder, phone strap or cable clips, so the collectibles are luck of the draw rather than something you can buy. The two things you can buy are a Shinchan Thermal Lunch Bag ($10.90, or $7.90 with a DBS/POSB card and $6.90 for Genki members) and a Shinchan hoodie at $25.90 that only members can get. Menu prices are before 10% service charge and GST, so the $3.20 taco is about $3.84 nett, and Genki's free app membership pays for itself on the lunch bag alone.

deals.body: Teachers, flash your ID this Friday. For Teachers' Day on 4 September 2026, three sister brands are running one-day-only treats at all outlets islandwide: Krispy Kreme gives a free half dozen Original Glazed with any dozen purchased (limited to 50 redemptions per store), llaollao upsizes 2 Medium Tubs to 2 Large Tubs free, and 108 Matcha Saro throws in a free soft serve with any 24-piece Warabi Mochi Box. All three need a Teacher's ID at the counter, are capped at one redemption per ID, and cannot stack with other promotions. One day only, while stocks last.

deals.body: IKEA Singapore is bringing back the dessert that looks like its most famous main course. From Friday 18 to Sunday 20 September 2026, the Swedish Bistro sells Swedish Meatball Ice Cream at $4.90: five meatball-shaped pieces of ice cream in a cup, with caramel sauce standing in for the cream sauce and IKEA's usual lingonberry jam on the side. IKEA's own bistro page calls it "back on demand" after its first run, and the only conditions it prints are the three dates, Swedish Bistro only, and while stocks last. That works out to 98 cents a piece, the same $4.90 the Tampines Level 1 bistro charges for four savoury meatballs in a cup. IKEA does not restrict it to one store, so all three bistro areas are in play, but two practical details decide where you go: the Level 1 bistro at Tampines runs a separate halal menu that does not list the dessert, and opening times differ by store, with Jurong starting earliest at 10am every day.

deals.body: TenRen's Tea Singapore is marking 9/13 with a 913 King's Oolong Sharing Day from Sunday 13 to Tuesday 15 September 2026: buy any two selected 913 Series tea drinks and the second cup is 50% off, and selected 913 retail items (the King's Oolong loose tea, the King's Tea bags and the 913 Chaffee drip-bag coffee on the poster) are 10% off. On two cups of the same price that is 25% off the pair, not half. The part to check before you travel: the brand's own announcement names no participating outlet, while one deal site lists The Star Vista only. TenRen's last two promos said "available at ALL outlets" or named The Star Vista outright, and this one does neither, so call ahead if you are heading to Bras Basah Complex or Funan.

Vouchers expire 14 October 2026 and none of it works online.

deals.body: At this point, you’re probably aware of most of the Haidilao freebies , but here’s a reminder. Finish off a lovely birthday evening with Haidilao ’s enormous complimentary birthday fruit platter . The spread consists of kiwi, seedless grapes, dragon fruit, and mangoes. If it’s for your grandparents, they’ll be treated to extra longevity buns for health and a long life. You’ll also be treated to a slice of cake plus a song from the staff. The best thing is, you don’t even need a membership, but do let them know in advance that it’s your birthday, so it’s easier for them to prepare. It’ll come with a whole birthday “performance”, but if the INFP within is screaming, you can ask the staff to do away with the whole song and dance.

deals.body: Those looking for a healthier treat to binge on can head to Tanuki Raw and get free slices of salmon sashimi according to age. Do note that you will also need to buy either 1 bottle of wine or a 720ml bottle of sake to wash all those salmon sashimi slices down. There is, however, a set limit of 40 slices, and no, your 80-year-old grandfather does not qualify for 2 separate sets of the maximum limit. Remember to also reserve a spot at least 24 hours before so they have time to prepare your special treat. This promo is only available at Tanuki Raw at Orchard Central. If you’re not a fan of seafood, fret not. Tanuki Raw’s Orchard Central outlet also has a birthday promotion where you can enjoy a complimentary bottle of merlot or chardonnay with a minimum spend of $60 . Do note that both promotions are valid from Mondays to Thursdays only.

deals.body: A shopping spree at MUJI can leave you feeling peckish, but also not wanting to spend any more than you just did. Good thing that you can get 15% off their cafe’s regular-priced a la carte dishes with a minimum of $10 spent. Their menu is on the healthier side, so you won’t have to worry about indulging in 2 pieces of their Hokkaido potato croquette. Otherwise, you can also choose from their cold deli menu’s assortment of salads. To sweeten your day further, you can also get 10% off their regular-priced clothes & household items with the same amount of minimum spend. Just remember to key in your birthdate in the Muji passport before your birth month, and you will get the discount coupon on the 10th of your birthday month.

members.title: Coffee Bean: 63% off Black Forest Mocha Ice Blended

members.body:
Finally, it has returned. I, like many other coffee lovers , have craved the comeback of the Black Forest Mocha Ice Blended from The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf .
That is why, for its 63rd anniversary in Singapore, Coffee Bean has brought it back for a limited time. If you’re a CoffeeBean SG Rewards member , you can even get the drink for 63% off until 21 Oct 2026 .
You’re probably familiar with the cake that shares the same name, but this drink is a fan favourite in its own right. So when it left the menu, many have been waiting for its return (me included). Now that it’s back, it comes with 2 whipped cream options: the classic and the new chocolate-flavoured one. Both are topped with chocolate curls.
CoffeeBean SG Rewards members can get 63% off 1 Black Forest Mocha Ice Blended , in Regular or Large size . This is available at all stores except those at Sentosa, Changi Airport, Jewel Changi Airport and Beanstro outlets.
The offer is open to new and existing members, with 1 redemption per member, so don’t worry if you haven’t signed up yet.
Of course, I went down to give it a try. Maybe it’s the nostalgia talking, but it’s exactly how I remember it — just cuter with the chocolate whipped cream!
The blend of rich, bitter mocha and sweet, vibrant maraschino cherries almost gives a Christmas-y vibe. The whipped cream is also light and not too sweet, making it a delightfully balanced drink.
That’s not all, though. From 13 Oct 2026 , you can get a free limited-edition canvas tote bag if you spend S$30 or more in a single in-store receipt. The tote comes with 3 stick-on patches from a collection of 18 artist-designed patches. Week 1 patches have been fully redeemed, unfortunately, but new designs will be released weekly while stocks last.
Week 2 starts on Tuesday, 20 Oct 2026 , so there’s still a chance to get one.
They also have a “ Scribble On ” contest on Instagram to encourage creativity in all of us. Share your doodles on Coffee Bean’s napkins, and you might just win a S$63 Coffee Bean e-gift card. The contest closes on 23 Oct 2026 , with entry instructions and terms on @coffeebeansg’s Instagram .
Free live caricature sessions with local artists @james.ek and @faizalcaricatures are also happening over 2 days. They’ll be at Causeway Point on Saturday, 17 Oct 2026 (3pm – 6pm) , and at Jem on Sunday , 18 Oct 2026 (3.30pm – 6.30pm) .
As you can tell, they really pulled out all the stops for Coffee Bean’s 63rd anniversary.
O’Coffee Club: Singapore’s heritage cafe since 1991 for artisanal coffee, dining & wine

links.title: Petra, a Mediterranean restaurant from ex-Ottolenghi and Aniba chefs, opens at Dempsey on 24 October

members.summary: Petra, a Mediterranean-Levantine restaurant at 40C Harding Road, opens at Dempsey Hill on 24 October. Former Aniba executive chef Anas Shami and ex-Ottolenghi head chef Dawid Nowosadzki lead the kitchen.
members.title: Petra opens at Dempsey Hill on 24 October with ex-Ottolenghi and Aniba chefs

members.body:
Dempsey gets a new Mediterranean restaurant this month, with chefs from Ottolenghi and Aniba behind the menu. Petra opens to the public on Saturday 24 October at 40C Harding Road, with a Levantine-leaning menu of mezze, wood-fired seafood and grilled meats, and reservations are already open.
Hummus is part of Petra’s mezze section, which opens on 24 October. Photo: Petra
The name comes from the ancient city carved out of rose-coloured stone in the Levant, and the cooking follows it: Mediterranean food from its eastern, Levantine end.
Who is cooking
Anas Shami is executive chef. He started in pastry and cooked in Berlin, Kyiv and Greece before joining the opening team of Aniba in Singapore, where he rose to executive chef.
Dawid Nowosadzki is consultant chef. He spent years in the Ottolenghi group, including head chef roles at NOPI and Ottolenghi in London, held senior roles at Soho House and an executive chef post in Doha, and most recently ran the kitchen at Koma, a vegetarian deli-restaurant in Hakushu, Japan. Vegetable-forward cooking is his calling card.
What is on the menu
Petra splits its food into three parts. The mezze section has house-made dips and freshly baked breads. Seafood and grilled meats come off the fire. A patisserie section covers Mediterranean-style sweets and seasonal desserts.
Hamachi tartare from Petra’s launch photographs. Photo: Petra
Hamachi tartare, hummus and muhallabia, a Middle Eastern milk pudding, are among the dishes in the restaurant’s own launch photographs.
Hours and booking
Petra is on Level 1 of 40C Harding Road, Dempsey Hill, Singapore 249548. It opens for lunch and dinner every day:
• Monday to Thursday: 11.30am to 3pm, and 5.30pm to 10.30pm
• Friday: 11.30am to 3pm, and 5.30pm to 11pm
• Saturday: 11.30am to 11pm, all day
• Sunday: 11.30am to 10.30pm, all day
Tables can be booked online through SevenRooms or by phone on +65 8876 5823. The restaurant also takes private dinners and long-table events.

Osteria Da Su is a new Italian-Korean restaurant in the CBD
Image credit: Osteria Da Su
If you’ve ever been torn between Korean and Italian food, Osteria Da Su is here to settle that conundrum. The Italian restaurant incorporates Korean flavours into its recipes, and will be opening its doors on 23 October 2026 along Telok Ayer Street.
Born in Korea, Chef Suji Park spent nearly a decade honing her culinary skills in Italy. Her passion for Italian cuisine shines through in her dishes, which also incorporate Korean influences that pay homage to her roots. Inspired by Italy’s laid-back dining culture, she envisioned the restaurant as a casual, welcoming space where diners can enjoy affordable Italian fare.
25 Telok Ayer Food Places For Famous Korean Fried Chicken, Orh Nee Tarts And More
The menu currently consists of 25 items that highlight Italian cooking techniques while featuring Korean flavours and ingredients. Starting with appetisers, highlights include the Zucchini Bruschetta ($12++) , a classic Italian dish with zucchini inspired by Korean banchan or side dishes. There’s also Insalata Condiglione ($18++) , a traditional Italian vegetable salad with a Korean soy-marinated egg.
Image credit: Osteria Da Su
On to the mains, the Tortelli Di Galbi Jjim ($30++) swaps out the classic meat filling of a traditional Italian tortelli with Korean braised pork, while the Farfalle All’Amatriciana ($24++) has gochujang bulgogi sauce brushed on the guanciale chips, finished with a pecorino cream.
The chef’s pick, however, is the Spaghetti Alle Vongole ($28++) , which is said to best showcase the Korean-Italian concept with the addition of asari clams, Korean parsley and more.
Image credit: Osteria Da Su
Finally, you can expect desserts such as a Salame Di Cioccolato ($10++) , inspired by Chef Suji’s Italian neighbours, and a Dalgona Tiramisu ($14++) . If dalgona sounds familiar, that’s because the traditional Korean candy was featured in the Netflix hit series, Squid Game .
Image credit: Osteria Da Su
The interior stays on theme, blending the minimalist aesthetic of contemporary Korean design with the warm tones of a classic Italian osteria.
Do note that as Osteria Da Su is in its soft opening phase, the opening hours may vary. We recommend checking its website for the latest hours before visiting.
If that wasn’t enough to satisfy your Korean food craving, browse the best Korean restaurants in Singapore. If you’re looking for desserts along Telok Ayer, AiFOKATO has a takeaway bar selling affogatos and more
Address: 163 Telok Ayer Street, Singapore 068616
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Osteria Da Su is not halal-certified.

Kiap Kiap is a new fried chicken bar in Bugis
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
My guilty pleasure after a late-night KTV sesh with my friends is almost always fried chicken. In fact, I’m probably Wingstop’s number one fan . My gripe, though, is that they close early, which isn’t ideal for my supper plans . If you’re like me, Kiap Kiap is a new fried chicken bar in Bugis you have to check out.
10 Best Late-Night Supper Spots In The East For Dim Sum, Wok Hei Ramen & More
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Decked out in retro-inspired red-and-white decor and LED lights, the space aims to create a vibey spot for people to connect over good food and drinks. There are even card games to keep you entertained if you ever get bored.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Food-wise, they specialise in all things fried chicken. Their signature Kiap Kiap’s Original Fried Chicken ($12++) features two pieces of golden-brown fried chicken. The chicken is said to be juicy and moist inside, while the exterior breading is shatteringly crunchy and seasoned with a secret blend of spices.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
If you’re looking to spice things up, there are also other fried chicken flavours to try. Mala addicts should definitely go for their Duck Fat Mala Fried Chicken ($14++) , comprising the same two pieces of fried chicken drenched in a spicy, savoury mala chilli oil made by simmering Sichuan peppercorns and other spices in duck fat.
Image credit: ANGELINE CHU SU LING via Google Maps
Those who can’t get enough of Genki Sushi’s mentaiko mayo should order the Mentaiko Fried Chicken With Ikura ($18++) , drizzled generously with creamy mentaiko mayo, then torched and garnished with ikura for a satisfying pop of flavour.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Fried chicken isn’t all that they serve, though, and it’ll be remiss of me to not share about their sides. Online reviews claim that their King’s Truffle Poutine ($20++) is a must-try: crispy yet fluffy fries topped with dollops of truffle mayo, a sunny-side-up fried egg, black truffle, and parmesan, all doused in umami beef gravy.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Get their Hot Mozzarella ($12++) for some seriously satisfying cheese pulls; here, you get stretchy mozzarella coated in a light breading and served with a tangy raspberry sauce for a sweet-and-savoury combo.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Otherwise, try their Seafood Jenny’s Udon ($16++) , a dish inspired by the founder’s mum. Meant to be shared round the table, it comes packed with springy udon noodles stir-fried with eggs and a medley of seafood, including scallops, squid, prawns, and octopus. It’s said to have a strong wok hei taste that’s reminiscent of hokkien mee .
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Round things off with the Banana Pudding ($6++) , served tableside: a heaping scoop of caramelised bananas and mascarpone sandwiched between layers of ladyfingers, topped with Biscoff cookie crumbs.
Image credit: @kiapkiap.sg
If cocktails are your thing, they’ve got a solid lineup of speciality drinks. Their signature, the Babygirl ($22++) , was originally curated by one of the founders for his wife, blending Patron Silver tequila with elderflower and raspberry.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Kiap Kiap also hosts monthly events. In October, they will be hosting Girl’s Night every Wednesday from 6pm to 11:30pm, which comes with free-flow truffle fries, 1-for-1 promotion for all gin and tonic beverages, and a complimentary tarot card reading with a minimum spend of $50 per person , just in time for the spooky season of Halloween!
The restaurant is a four-minute walk away from Bugis MRT Station .
My hot take: Based on personal experience, the earthy notes of matcha balance out the richness of fried chicken, so after your meal, get your matcha fix at Little Rituals , located a nine-minute walk away. If you’re not so adventurous, you can check out our guide to the best food in Bugis instead for more eats in the locale.
Address: 1 Liang Seah Street, #02-15, Singapore 189022
Opening hours: Sun-Thurs 5:30pm to 1am, Fri-Sat 5:30pm to 2am
Website
Kiap Kiap is not halal-certified.

Kinki Restaurant + Bar at Customs House puts Oita Wagyu, Himeshima tiger prawns and yellowtail on a six-dish limited menu from 15 to 31 October, with plates from S$12 to S$68 before service charge and GST. The A Taste of Oita menu is ordered a la carte, not as a set, so a table can add one dish to a regular dinner or order the lot.
The A Taste of Oita menu runs at Kinki from 15 to 31 October. Photo: Kinki Restaurant + Bar
Oita sits on the north-east coast of Kyushu, the prefecture behind Beppu’s hot springs and the kabosu, a sharp green citrus it grows more of than anywhere else in Japan. Both turn up in the dish names.
The six dishes and what they cost
• Jigoku Ribeye, S$68: seared Oita Wagyu with seasonal local vegetables, smoked Japanese burrata and a spicy hot sauce butter
• Kabosu Coast, S$24: yellowtail ceviche with leche de tigre, papadum chips and Secai Marche Japanese burrata
• Tiger Nashi, S$18: gyoza filled with Himeshima tiger prawns and Hita pears, with a pineapple chipotle sauce
• Shiitake Claypot, S$32: braised sweet Oita shiitake with assorted mushrooms over butter rice
• Himeshima “Hae” Mee, S$18: tiger prawns in Japanese udon, done Singapore-style
• Sweet Potato O’ Mine, S$12: a tart made with Oita sweet potato, topped with cheese mousse
Himeshima “Hae” Mee swaps yellow noodles for udon, at S$18. Photo: Kinki Restaurant + Bar
Where the menu leans
Jigoku means hell, the name Beppu gives its boiling hot spring pools, and the ribeye is the one dish built to match it with a spicy butter. It is also the only one over S$35, so most of the menu sits at small-plate prices.
The two prawn dishes are the most Singaporean ideas on the card. Hae mee is a prawn noodle dish most readers will know from a hawker centre; here it swaps yellow noodles for udon and uses prawns from Himeshima, a small island off Oita’s coast. The gyoza pairs the same prawns with pears from Hita, an inland Oita city.
Burrata appears twice, in the ribeye and the ceviche, both times a Japanese-made cheese.
How it compares with the regular menu
The Oita dishes are priced close to Kinki’s everyday dinner card. The Shiitake Claypot is S$2 more than the restaurant’s Magic Mushroom Claypot at S$30, and the Kabosu Coast ceviche is S$2 less than the Hamachi Crudo, another yellowtail starter, at S$26.
The regular Ohmi Wagyu Hoba-yaki, an A4 striploin with mushrooms, is S$90 for one person, against S$68 for the Oita cut. The prawn gyoza is S$18, against S$32 for the Wagyu Foie Gras Gyoza on the main menu.
The Shiitake Claypot is S$32, S$2 more than Kinki’s regular mushroom claypot. Photo: Kinki Restaurant + Bar
The claypot is the one meat-free-looking main, though the menu carries no vegetarian, halal or allergen labels.
Booking and getting there
Kinki takes reservations on its website. The restaurant is in Customs House on Collyer Quay, a short walk from Raffles Place MRT, with the Kinki rooftop bar upstairs. The Oita dishes are served at the restaurant from Thursday 15 October until Saturday 31 October.

Tokyo Onigiri opens in Singapore at One Raffles Place
Image credit: @tokyo_onigiri_sg
Raffles Place lunch crowd: there’s a new onigiri option in the basement. Tokyo Onigiri , a Japanese rice ball specialist, recently opened its first Singapore outlet at One Raffles Place , with onigiri starting from $4.90. The shop is takeaway only, and the mall connects directly to Raffles Place MRT Station , so it’s an easy grab on the way back to the office.
Raffles Place Food Guide: 17 Places For Korean Cai Png, Famous Roast Meat And More
For the uninitiated, Tokyo Onigiri is the overseas arm of Ichiryu Manpuku, a Tokyo-based onigiri specialist founded by Yuka Hayakawa in 2023. The original Tokyo outlet is known for its fluffy, lightly shaped onigiri, with around 20 fillings to choose from. Its bestseller is the Grilled Salmon and Salmon Roe Onigiri (¥650) . The brand has since expanded to Mongolia and Taiwan, with Singapore marking its sixth outlet.
Image credit: @onigiri_ichiryu_manpuku
Ordering takes three steps. First, pick your format: the 2-Onigiri Set Meal (from $13.90) , the 3-Onigiri Set Meal (from $18.80) , or a la carte onigiri (from $4.90) . These prices are for Classic fillings. Popular, Signature, Premium, and Double Fillings upgrades are available for a higher price.
Image credit: @onigiri_ichiryu_manpuku
Next, choose your fillings. You can mix up to two fillings in a single onigiri. Finally, set meals come with a choice of miso soup or a canned drink, plus a side of pickled cucumber or pickled daikon.
Image credit: @tokyo_onigiri_sg
If you’re not sure what to pick, start with the shop’s six featured combinations. The cheapest in this series are the Soy Glazed Meat & Soy Marinated Egg Yolk ($7.90) and the Kimchi Pork & Soy Marinated Egg Yolk ($7.90) .
Image credit: @tokyo_onigiri_sg
Three combinations sit at $8.90 each: the Sukiyaki & Soy Marinated Egg Yolk ($8.90) , the Salmon Mayo with Yuzu Kosho & Mentaiko ($8.90) , and the Hotate Soy Butter & Mentaiko ($8.90) . The priciest is the Roasted Salmon & Ikura ($9.90) .
Do note that the kiosk is takeaway-only, so you’ll have to dabao your onigiri back to the office if you’re grabbing lunch.
If you’re keen on more rice balls, read our Onigiri GON feature on a Fukuoka-run counter at Fortune Centre.
You can also check out our guide to the best Japanese restaurants in Singapore .
Address: 1 Raffles Place, #B1-36, One Raffles Place, Singapore 048616
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11am to 7pm, Sat 10am to 3pm
Website
Tokyo Onigiri is not halal-certified.

Ginza-famous Age.3 is opening in Singapore this November
Image credit: @age.3_ginza
Sando fans, take note: Age.3 , the Japanese fried sando specialist that’s gone viral for its crisp, golden sandwiches, is opening its first Singapore outlet at ION Orchard in mid-November 2026 .
20 Japanese Cafes In Singapore For Loaded Sando, Matcha On Tap And More
Image credit: @age.3_ginza
Since opening its Ginza store in December 2023, Age.3 has sold more than one million fried sandos worldwide, with queues at the Ginza shop reaching up to two hours. Each sando is fried and filled to order with Japanese milk bread baked fresh daily, giving it a crisp, golden exterior and a soft, chewy centre.
Image credit: @age.3_ginza
The Singapore menu will feature 34 sweet and savoury varieties. On the sweet side, the classic Whipped Cream Sando (price TBD) is made with low-sugar fresh whipped cream that’s prepared in-store and whipped by hand. Other flavours include the Chocolate Strawberry (price TBD) , Mandarin Orange (price TBD) , Mont Blanc (price TBD) , and Creme Brulee Sando (price TBD) .
Image credit: @age.3_ginza
If you prefer something savoury, consider ordering the Beef Short Rib Yakiniku Sando (price TBD) , which comes with a special barbecue sauce and is topped with a soft-cooked egg. There’s also the Grilled Keema Curry (price TBD) , Chicken Nanban (price TBD) , and Grilled Cheese with Smoked Salmon (price TBD) .
While we don’t have prices for the upcoming SG outlet, the sandwiches usually cost between ¥650 to ¥850 in Japan, which works out to roughly $5.30 to $6.90 at current exchange rates. Do note that prices here may differ.
The exact opening date has yet to be announced, but we’ll update this article with more information once we have it.
In other exciting food news, Tokyo Onigiri has opened its first Singapore outlet at One Raffles Place, with onigiri from $4.90. If you’re craving more Japanese food, the Japan Rail Fair 2026 returns to Guoco Tower from 15 October to 17 October, with free admission and regional treats such as Hokkaido dairy and fresh Japanese pears.
Address: ION Orchard, Singapore 238801
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Age.3 is not halal-certified.

It is best suited for CBD office workers seeking a quiet, budget-friendly lunch, though early visits are recommended as popular dishes often sell out before the end of peak hours.

members.body:
Opus Bar & Grill has 1-for-1 Sunday buffet with Old Chang Kee
Image credit: Opus Bar & Grill
Sunday buffet plans just got easier on the wallet. Opus Bar & Grill is teaming up with Old Chang Kee for the Curry On! Sunday Local Lunch Buffet , and adults get a 1-for-1 deal on it.
11 Best 1-For-1 Buffet Deals In 2026, From $28++ Per Person
The buffet runs every Sunday from now until 29 November 2026 , from 12pm to 3pm . Adult buffets cost $108++ for two , which works out to $54++ per person when you bring a buddy.
Image credit: @vocoorchardsg
The main draw is the Old Chang Kee Corner, where the brand’s curry chicken and chilli crab flavours show up in dishes you wouldn’t expect. There’s Laksa Infused Popiah , Nasi Lemak Lobster Kueh Pie Tee , and a Nasi Lemak Seaweed Roll .
Image credit: @vocoorchardsg
Mains include Chilli Crab Pizza , Curry Chicken Pizza , Curry Chicken Lasagna , Laksa Roast Salmon , and Laksa Marinated Popcorn Chicken . Purists can still grab Old Chang Kee’s classic Curry Chicken Potato Puff !
Image credit: @vocoorchardsg
Beyond the collab dishes, the spread is packed with hawker staples. At the noodle station, you’ll find the restaurant’s Signature Laksa with Rock Lobster and Mee Rebus with Beef Balls . There’s even a live Oyster Omelette station, Chicken Satay , and a DIY Rojak counter with you tiao and fresh fruit.
Meat lovers get a roasted meat station with roast duck , soy-poached chicken , and Hainanese steamed chicken served with ginger rice.
Image credit: Sailaway Lounge via Google Maps
Dim sum fans can look forward to Curry Chicken Siew Mai and Kaya Pau , along with street food options including Nyonya Asam Fish , and Five-Spice Braised Beef Brisket .
For dessert, expect Red Bean Soup with Dried Tangerine Peel and assorted Nyonya kueh . There’s also a selection from D9 Cakery, including its Signature D9 Cakery Cheesecake and D9 Cakery Carrot Pound Cake .
Image credit: Opus Bar & Grill
The buffet includes free-flow still and sparkling water, speciality coffee, and artisanal tea. Kids aged six to 12 pay $28++ per child , while children aged five and below dine free.
Prefer a drink with your meal? Alcohol is available as an add-on, with options such as Ruggeri Prosecco , beer , house wine , zero-proof wine , and cocktails , affordably priced at $10++ per glass. There’s also a free-flow alcohol option going for $48++ per person .
If you’re after more ways to eat out for less, check out our guide to the best food deals in October 2026 . You can also read our guide to the best buffets in Singapore for more free-flow options!
Address: 581 Orchard Road, Singapore 238883 (a short walk from Orchard MRT Station)
Buffet hours: Sun 12pm to 2:30pm
Tel: 6730 3390
Website
Opus Bar & Grill is not halal-certified.

deals.body:
Two hotel buffet rooms have given their dinner spreads over to Halloween, and on 31 October itself both charge S$118++ an adult. Lime at PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering runs its SubLIME Halloween buffet for 10 nights from 23 October, while The Line at Shangri-La Singapore holds a one-night Halloween dinner buffet on Saturday 31 October.
Photo: PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering
Both lay out seafood on ice with Boston lobster and snow crab, and both serve pork, so neither is halal. The real split is the calendar. Lime is the only one of the two with a weeknight price, and The Line is a Halloween-night booking or nothing.
Lime, PARKROYAL COLLECTION Pickering
SubLIME Halloween runs daily from 23 October to 1 November, 6pm to 9.30pm, with last order at 9pm. Monday to Thursday is S$88++ an adult and S$44++ a child. Friday and Saturday is S$118++ and S$59++, and Sunday is S$108++ and S$54++. Coffee and tea are included.
The S$30 weekend premium buys specific dishes. A whole baby lamb from the barbecue, Nordic whole salmon, curry crab with mantou and a lobster bisque risotto finished in a Parmesan wheel are on Friday to Sunday only. Monday to Thursday gets a Bloody Mary lobster pasta in the Parmesan wheel instead.
The rest stays all week: black garlic-glazed beef short rib at the carving station, Josper-grilled pork ribs and sausages, a Peranakan corner with chef Alvin’s beef rendang, crab meat kueh pie tee and sambal stingray with okra, a Penang prawn noodle station and a chocolate fountain.
Children aged 6 to 12 pay the child price and children aged 5 and below eat free. Pan Pacific DISCOVERY members get up to 25 per cent off dining, and early bookings save up to 20 per cent. Lime is at 3 Upper Pickering Street, a short walk from Chinatown MRT station. Bookings are on WhatsApp at +65 9859 0681 or by phone at +65 3138 2251.
The Line, Shangri-La Singapore
A Wicked Feast is dinner on Saturday 31 October only, from 6pm to 9.30pm, at S$118++ an adult and S$59++ a child aged 6 to 11.
Photo: Shangri-La Singapore. The Line’s Halloween buffet is on 31 October only, S$118++ an adult.
Alongside lobster, snow crab, sea prawns and sashimi, there is a black truffle mushroom beef Wellington and a bone-in lamb leg at the carving station, beef tongue with golden polenta, a seafood barbecue with grilled prawns and baked oyster mornay, an Arabic station with veal and chicken shawarma, and an Indian section with binchotan tandoori chicken and lamb biryani. Desserts include a Musang King durian cake.
Pork appears in the roast pork belly, the ma la pork intestine and the charcuterie.
The child band is the catch for families. A 12-year-old pays the child price at Lime but the adult price at The Line, so two adults and a 12-year-old on Halloween night pay S$295++ at Lime and S$354++ at The Line.
Shangri-La’s 40 per cent flash deal and Shangri-La Circle points redemption do not apply, though members still earn points. The Line is at Shangri-La Singapore, 22 Orange Grove Road, and takes bookings on (65) 6213 4398.

members.body:
Pastamania has 1-for-1 pasta promo for a limited time
For many of us, Pastamania was probably our first intro to Italian food . I remember heading there with my friends after school because it was that affordable, especially for a student. Even as adults, they’re forever giving us reasons to go back. This time, they’re running their annual 1-for-1 promo on all pasta dishes from 19 October to 23 October 2026 in celebration of World Pasta Day.
That means you can jio a friend and score two pasta mains for the price of one. The promo applies to all pasta, even fan favourites such as their Spaghetti Carbonara (U.P. $13.50) , spicy Arrabbiata (U.P. $8.50) , and hearty Beef Meatballs Pasta (U.P. $13) . The cheapest mains are the Pomodoro , Aglio Olio , and Cheesy Crumble , which go for $7.90 before the discount. With the 1-for-1 deal, you’re only paying $3.95 for each portion—a steal in this economy!
44 Best Italian Restaurants In Singapore For All Budgets—$7.90 Pasta, Fried Pizza And More
The promo runs from opening till 5pm daily, with last orders at 4:45pm. Each table can redeem up to two free pasta dishes, so you’ll want to plan your orders accordingly.
View this post on Instagram
Do note that the offer is valid for dine-in and takeaway orders made over the counter. But they’re not valid at Pastamania Pronto outlets.
The promo runs for four days only, so be sure to check their full list of eateries before heading down!
If you’re craving more deals, check out Spicy Hubby’s 1-For-1 Nasi Lemak promo at The Centrepoint in Orchard or our comprehensive guide to the best 1-for-1 buffet deals in 2026 , starting from just $28++ per person .
For more affordable Italian food, read our review of Vincenzo Capuano’s $28++ unlimited pizza and pasta buffet to see how it fared. You really don’t have to bust your budget to eat well.

deals.body:
Calendar Coffee is a new cafe in Chinatown with matcha and bakes
Image credit: Damaine Teo via Google Maps
Coffee lovers, here’s a new spot to add to your cafe-hopping list! The folks behind June Coffee have just opened a new cafe, Calendar Coffee , which is a two-minute walk from Maxwell MRT Station . The cosy cafe has a charming cottagecore aesthetic, complete with muted colours, wooden furniture, and homely decor.
Image credit: Calendar Coffee via Google Maps
While the cafe doesn’t offer any mains, the menu features a selection of desserts and drinks. The French toast series is definitely their most unique offering. Flavours include Apple Pie ($11++), Blueberry Cheesecake ($12++), and even savoury options such as Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese ($14++).
You’ll also find chiffon cakes ($12++) by the slice, available in three flavours: Black Sesame, Earl Grey Strawberry, and Banoffee . They also offer cookies ($6++) in Brown Butter Chocolate Chip, Buttered Toast and Jam, and Malted Milk and Cereal flavours
Image credit: Calendar Coffee via Google Maps
Pair the food with some drinks—signatures at the cafe include Roasted Rice Latte ($9++), Jasmine Apple Americano ($8.50++), Miso Caramel Hojicha ($9++), and Osmanthus Mochi Matcha ($9.50++).
Image credit: Calendar Coffee via Google Maps
If you’re not feeling adventurous, they also have the classics, including Double Espresso ($5++) and Latte ($7++) . Choose between two coffee bean selections: Stories from Myanmar or La Reforma Santa Ana from El Salvador, for a top-up of $1++.
Matcha and tea lovers are not forgotten—the cafe also offers Matcha Latte ($6.50++), Hojicha Latte ($6++), and Strawberry Matcha Latte ($8.50++) , as well as cold brews and hot teas. They offer three types of matcha powder: Yabukita , Premium Yabukita (+$2.50++), and Asanoka (+$5++).
Do note that the cafe can get pretty crowded, so be prepared to wait a little!
If you’re on the hunt for more matcha spots, read our ranked list of best matcha cafes in Singapore . Otherwise, read our Chinatown food itinerary for more good food in the area.
Address : 258 South Bridge Road, #01-01, Singapore 058807
Opening hours: Tue-Sun 11am to 6pm
Website
Calendar Coffee is not halal-certified.

deals.body: Up to 61% off Giant has refreshed its Tampines Hypermarket at 21 Tampines North Drive 2 and is marking the reopening with a week of store-only specials, Thursday 15 to Wednesday 21 October 2026. The four-day fresh deals (15 to 18 Oct) put extra-large Vannamei prawns at $1 per 100g (was $2.29), whole fresh salmon at $1.49 per 100g and a tray of 30 eggs at $4.85, which is 10 cents below FairPrice's capped $4.95 tray. All week, 24 cans of Coca-Cola are $10.95 (was $21.15), Korean Shine Muscat grapes are $10.45 for 800g (was $20.90), two bottles of Four Cousins wine are $19.80 (was $52), and seven lines are Buy 1 Get 1 Free. The first 300 shoppers each day from 15 to 18 Oct who spend $50 nett in one receipt, from 11am, get a free yuu reusable bag. The catch: the prices are for the Tampines Hypermarket only, the fresh deals stop on Sunday 18 Oct, eggs are capped at 2 trays per customer, and everything is while stocks last.

members.body:
KFC Samyang Buldak Carbonara returns with new macaroni bowl
PSA to all fried chicken and spice lovers: KFC Singapore has brought back their KFC x Samyang Buldak Carbonara collab from earlier this year, with a new item on the roster this time.
Image credit: KFC
From 21 October 2026 , you can order their new Samyang Buldak Carbonara Macaroni Bowl for just $5.50 . Expect mac and cheese tossed in a creamy Samyang Buldak Carbonara-infused cheese sauce, topped with crispy popcorn chicken bites. To amp things up even more, you can order an extra side of Samyang Buldak Carbonara Sauce (price TBD) .
If you’re worried about the spice, fret not: each bowl comes with a free upgrade to a medium Sprite , giving you more to sip on between bites to cool down.
The fan favourite Samyang Buldak Carbonara Loaded Fries is also making a comeback: golden-brown fries slathered in KFC’s iconic cheese sauce and Samyang Carbonara sauce for a spicy kick. The creamy, slightly sweet cheese sauce helped to mellow out some of the spice, while fresh spring onions cut through the richness. They’re $5.65 a la carte, or $3.95 when added to a meal.
Image credit: Roger Ng (iUnspoken) via Google Maps
The KFC x Samyang Buldak Carbonara menu is available for a limited time at all KFC outlets islandwide, except for Jewel, Sentosa, Singapore Polytechnic, and Singapore Zoo, while stocks last. Do take note that these menu items are not available on public holidays.
KFC x Samyang Buldak isn’t the only thing making a comeback right now: McDonald’s McGriddles are also back on the menu for a limited time! Otherwise, if fast food isn’t your thing, check out our guide to the best food deals in October .
Website | Full list of outlets

members.body:
Spicy Hubby opens at The Centrepoint with Nasi Ayam Gepuk
Popular Nasi Lemak stall Spicy Wife is bringing her husband into the picture. The stall, which opened in 2022, built a cult-like following at Amoy Street Food Centre for its aromatic nasi lemak and generous portions. Now it’s bringing those beloved flavours to The Centrepoint under a new name, Spicy Hubby , so you can check out the hype from the comfort of an air-conditioned mall.
Even better, the new eatery is holding a 1-for-1 opening promotion between 16 October and 18 October, so grab a friend and don’t miss out!
Menu-wise, Spicy Hubby features the brand’s signature dish alongside two exclusive new dishes. The signature Nasi Goreng Ayam Berempah ($9.90) comes with fried chicken, coconut rice, and a dollop of sambal sauce. The highlight is the crispy and fragrant chicken, said to be marinated overnight in a rempah of eight ingredients.
While classics are hard to beat, the new dishes sound just as good—the Nasi Rendang Ayam ($12.90) features rendang chicken slow-cooked in a thick coconut gravy, while the Nasi Ayam Gepuk ($12.90) features hand-pounded, marinated fried chicken that’s said to be tender yet crisp and bursting with flavour.
You can also spice up your meal with a variety of sides. Options include XL Otak ($4.90) , a grilled fish paste, Fried Tempe ($4.90) , fermented soybeans, Okra Curry ($2.90), Fried Sunny Side Up ($1.50) , Curry Fish Ball ($6.90) and more.
For some extra crunch, consider the Long Bean Sambal ($2.90), Fried Prawn Cracker ($1.90), and Fried Shrimp Roll ($6.90).
Wash it all down with a refreshing Sparkling Calamansi for $4.90.
To find out the best nasi lemak in town (in our opinion), read our ranked list of the best nasi lemak in Singapore. Alternatively, if you just want to indulge in Malaysian cuisine, check out these 30 Malaysian food places.
Address: 76 Orchard Road, #01-55/56, The Centrepoint Food Street, Singapore 238843
Opening Hours: Daily 10am to 9pm
Website
Spicy Hubby is not halal-certified but uses no pork or lard.
