Shan Li You opens in Jewel Changi Airport with Yunnan cuisine
Image credits: Jewel Changi Airport
Changi Airport is known to be a haven for shopping and good eats, and Jewel just got even more happening with the recent arrival of Shan Li You , a restaurant hailing from Yunnan serving authentic dishes cooked by veteran local chefs.
Changi Airport Food Guide: 38 Places To Dine At Before Catching Your Flight
Image credits: Jewel Changi Airport
The brand prides itself on using the freshest ingredients and staying true to Yunnan’s ethnic roots through its extensive offerings. The menu spans savoury, spicy, and sweet dishes inspired by the brand’s mountain-to-table concept.
Fans of Shan Li You rave about the Porcini Mushroom, Truffle and Egg Rice (price TBD) as a must-order dish for your visit here. Not only is it packed with a strong and fragrant truffle aroma, but it’s also loaded with fresh porcini mushrooms for an extra bite in each mouthful. Break the golden egg yolk on top for a creamy sauce that coats each grain of rice perfectly!
Image credit: Jewel Changi Airport
For something more refreshing, try the Wild Pepper and Wild Fruit Sour Beef Soup (price TBD) . Tender cuts of sliced beef marinated with spices give the hearty broth a spicy kick in every sip, while the wild fruit adds a bold, tangy flavour.
Image credit: @yum_seng
Based on reviews online, a crowd-favourite appears to be the Lychee Sweet and Sour Pork (price TBD) , featuring a massive passionfruit in the middle of the plate. We’re guessing the lychee acts as a natural sweetener, while the passionfruit adds a tangy kick that gives the dish a more layered flavour.
Image credit: Jewel Changi Airport
Pair your meal with their variety of drinks, too. Here, you can create your own pot of tea for just $1.90++ per person with four flavours to choose from: Yunnan Rose Tea , Golden Chrysanthemum Tea , Sticky Rose Green Tea and Rice Pu’er Tea . Do note that there’s a minimum of two people to order, so you’ll have to dine with a buddy to try this out. If tea isn’t up your alley, you can opt for one of their fresh fruit ice-blended drinks instead.
While we’ve yet to get our hands on Shan Li You’s menu and prices, we’ll update this article once we have more information. In the meantime, do head down and give them a try for yourselves!
For more spots to eat at in the airport, read our guide to the best food in Jewel . If you happen to be catching a red-eye flight soon, our comprehensive guide to the best 24/7 eateries in Changi Airport will save you from midnight hunger pangs.
Address: 78 Airport Boulevard, #02-217, Singapore 819666
Opening hours: Mon-Fri 11:30am to 10pm, Sat-Sun 11am to 10pm
Tel: 8821 0250
Shan Li You is not halal-certified.

Sushiro has put three premium plates on a limited menu across its Singapore restaurants from 7 October to 3 November 2026.
Sushiro’s limited premium-plate menu runs to 3 November 2026. Photo: Sushiro Singapore
Sushiro Singapore prices the Aburi Wild Blackthroat Seaperch at S$3.90++, Sous Vide Tender Roast Beef at S$5.90++, and Bancha Braised Octopus at S$3.90++, while stocks last. Prices differ at the Mandai Wildlife Reserve Digiro outlet.
What is on the plate
The seaperch is lightly salted and gently seared for a fatty, umami finish. The roast beef is seasoned with salt and slow-cooked sous vide to keep it tender. The octopus uses Hokkaido mizudako boiled in bancha, roasted green tea, so the tea aroma sits beside the seafood rather than covering it.
The limited plates sit on top of Sushiro’s usual conveyor-belt list of more than 100 sushi and side dishes. Diners still order by touchscreen or from the belt as usual; the three items are the dated add-ons for this window.
Outlets and timing
Orchard Gateway’s Sushiro is at 227 Orchard Road, #B1-07/08. Hougang Mall at 90 Hougang Avenue 10, #02-23/24, opens on 1 October 2026. Most mall outlets run 11am to 10pm with last order at 9.30pm; Jewel Changi opens from 10am.
The premium-plate run continues islandwide at participating restaurants through 3 November, or until stocks run out. The regular menu runs from tuna and grilled salmon to ramen and desserts, with seasonal Japanese specials rotating through the year.
Booking a table
Reservations are taken only through the Sushiro mobile app, where diners pick an arrival time and get a queue number in advance. Takeaway is available at the outlets. The chain opened Japan’s first conveyor-belt sushi restaurant in 1984 and now serves more than 100 varieties of fresh sushi, ramen, desserts and seasonal specials in Singapore.

deals.body:
Potatoes are a beloved staple for many, myself included. With their versatility, you can cook them in so many ways — boiled, mashed, fried — you name it, it probably yields delicious results. If your favourite potato dish is rosti , you’ll be happy to hear that Hippopotato has opened its first physical store in Punggol .
Previously a popular home-based business selling a large variety of rosti with 5.0 stars across 516 Google reviews (at the time of writing), the owners have decided to open up shop in Northshore Plaza I . Their original home-based outlet in Tampines will be closed until further notice, with plans to resume business there once the Punggol store can run independently.
The rosti store is helmed by 2 brothers, Gary Wong and James Wong. Born into a family of cooks and hawkers, the brothers said in an Instagram post , “Food has always been a big part of our DNA”. Hence, they started Hippopotato in 2025 with the goal of making yummy rosti accessible to all.
Fun fact: They used to run a cai fan stall at a Junior College. Plus, James used to be a Marche chef at, you guessed it… the rosti station. Without further ado, here’s what I tried at Hippopotato.
I started with their Golden Classic Rosti (S$5) and opted for sour cream. The usual price for this is S$8 , but to celebrate their grand opening, the first 50 customers can get it for S$5 . This promotion runs from 15 to 18 Oct 2026 , while stocks last.
The rostis were made to order, thus having a perfectly crisp exterior with a nice char that added smokiness to every bite. The potatoes were soft and delicate on the interior, creating a nice medley of textures. When topped with the sour cream, it adds a piquancy to the mild dish. Personally, I prefer it with a heaping spoonful of the sour cream.
The next rosti I tried was the O konomirosti (S$10.50) . This dish is the lovechild of popular Japanese dish o konomiyaki and rosti , inheriting the positives of both parents. As you can see in the picture above, Hippopotato is extremely generous with the bonito flakes given.
Beneath the flakes are also generous drizzles of tangy okonomiyaki sauce and Japanese mayonnaise. This was my favourite as each bite just brought such intense goodness to my taste buds. Bold and savoury from the bonito flakes and okonomiyaki sauce, slightly creamy from the mayonnaise — just wow.
Aside from rosti , Hippopotato also has a range of potato-based sides, such as tater tots and fries. I opted for the Mentaiko Mayo Tater Tots (S$5) . I’m a huge mentaiko fan, but I find typical mentaiko sauces lack the same umami as the actual pollack roe.
Luckily for me, the sauce hits the spot. Slightly spicy with a rich, briny flavour, it complemented the crispy tater tots well. The only thing I wished for was more sauce; there’s an option for the sauce to be on the side for an additional S$0.30, which I will probably go for in the future.
Would I recommend Hippopotato ? Definitely. With amazing rosti and sides, why not #supportlocal while enjoying good food?

The next rosti I tried was the O konomirosti (S$10.50) . This dish is the lovechild of popular Japanese dish o konomiyaki and rosti , inheriting the positives of both parents. As you can see in the picture above, Hippopotato is extremely generous with the bonito flakes given.
Beneath the flakes are also generous drizzles of tangy okonomiyaki sauce and Japanese mayonnaise. This was my favourite as each bite just brought such intense goodness to my taste buds. Bold and savoury from the bonito flakes and okonomiyaki sauce, slightly creamy from the mayonnaise — just wow.
Aside from rosti , Hippopotato also has a range of potato-based sides, such as tater tots and fries. I opted for the Mentaiko Mayo Tater Tots (S$5) . I’m a huge mentaiko fan, but I find typical mentaiko sauces lack the same umami as the actual pollack roe.
Luckily for me, the sauce hits the spot. Slightly spicy with a rich, briny flavour, it complemented the crispy tater tots well. The only thing I wished for was more sauce; there’s an option for the sauce to be on the side for an additional S$0.30, which I will probably go for in the future.
Would I recommend Hippopotato ? Definitely. With amazing rosti and sides, why not #supportlocal while enjoying good food?
10 must-try food stalls at Punggol Coast Hawker Centre

The menu features freshly made potato rosti, including the Golden Classic Rosti (S$8) and Okonomirosti (S$10.50), alongside sides such as Mentaiko Mayo Tater Tots (S$5). It is a useful option for Punggol residents and potato lovers seeking affordable, locally made comfort food.

Bari Bari Grand has opened at Arcade @ The Capitol Kempinski, bringing the brand’s premium teppan format a short walk from City Hall MRT after its Tampines debut earlier this year. Bari Bari Steak positions the Capitol outlet as its Grand line: Japanese A4 and A5 Miyazaki wagyu cuts and seafood, finished on a 300°C hot stone at the table, with free-flow access to a Japanese gourmet bar on every teppan order.
Photo: Bari Bari Steak
Capitol Singapore puts the restaurant at 15 Stamford Road, open daily from 11am to 10pm. Bari Bari Grand is at #01-82 Arcade @ The Capitol Kempinski, Singapore 178906, with bookings on 6284 3788.
Hot stone, then the bar
Each teppan plate arrives with a high-density Japanese stone heated to 300°C, so diners can take the meat from the house medium-rare finish to their preferred doneness. Steaks come crowned with a house herb butter. The complimentary gourmet bar rotates salads, seasonal starters and Japanese-inspired bites for the table.
Photo: Bari Bari Steak
A sashimi add-on menu is available.
How it sits against the first outlet
Bari Bari Grand is the premium offshoot of Bari Bari Steak. Tampines came first in January; Capitol is the city second stop. The format stays interactive rather than chef-only teppanyaki: diners finish the cut on the stone, then graze the bar without a separate buffet ticket.
City Hall MRT exits onto Stamford Road. The Capitol Kempinski arcade sits on the same block as the hotel lobby shops. The restaurant is not halal-certified.

It’s time for celebration , especially for those with a sweet tooth . Drips Bakery recently turned 16 years old and is marking the occasion with new French-inspired bakes and savoury creations .
Credit: Drips Bakery
At the centre of the celebration is the Tart Medley (S$46.60 , U.P. S$56 ) , a collection of 6 French butter-baked tarts in one shareable box . If you’re heading to a party or potluck , this is a delightful sweet treat to bring along.
The 6 flavours featured in the box are Blackberry Crumble , Macadamia , Cherry Brandy , Cinnamon Apple , French Pear , and Cinnamon Raspberry . The Tart Medley is available for a limited time from 13 October 2026 to 31 December 2026 , so get your hands on it before the year ends.
Credit: Drips Bakery
For those of you who prefer something more savoury, consider trying another 2 new creations at Drips Bakery: Charcoal Sea Salt Butter Ciabatta and Fried Onion & Herbs Ciabatta .
These new ciabatta items are priced at S$6.80 each or S$11.60 for a pair of both flavours .
Credit: Drips Bakery
From 13 October 2026 to 31 December 2026 , there will also be an anniversary promotion you can make use of when visiting Drips Bakery. Purchase any pair of 8” sliced tarts for just S$16 , instead of the usual S$8.80–S$9.80 per slice.
Love tarts and bakes? Now’s the best time to enjoy some!

deals.body:
Colony, the buffet restaurant at The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, has turned its seven kitchens over to a Japan Week menu until Sunday 25 October, with prices from S$108++ for weekday lunch to S$998++ for a Sunday brunch poured with Cristal. The Japan Week started on 16 October and covers every lunch, dinner and brunch session in the 10 days.
Japan Week runs at Colony from 16 to 25 October 2026. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
The menus mix izakaya-style Japanese dishes into Colony’s usual international and local spread rather than replacing it. The Ice Bar, The Grill and Rotisserie, The Steam Basket, The Wok, The Tandoor, The Fruit Stall and The Patisserie all stay open, and the local roast meats and wok dishes are still on the line.
Four price points, four menus
Each session has its own Japan Week menu, and the price climbs with the seafood.
• Lunch, Monday to Saturday, 12pm to 2.30pm: S$108++ an adult, S$54++ for children aged six to 12. Sashimi, nigiri, a truffle tuna roll and chilled buckwheat noodles, plus kimchi pork fried rice and pork belly yaki udon from The Wok.
• Dinner, Sunday to Thursday, 6pm to 10.30pm: S$130++ an adult, S$65++ a child. Adds freshly shucked oysters, snow crab, a negitoro avocado bruschetta, chashu omurice, menchi katsu and tori karaage with nanban sauce.
• Seafood dinner, Friday and Saturday, 6pm to 10.30pm: S$152++ an adult, or S$250++ with free-flow Barons de Rothschild Ritz Réserve Brut NV Champagne; S$76++ a child. Adds langoustine, kaki furai fried oysters, unagi omurice, a truffle seafood okonomiyaki and Singapore chilli crab with golden mantou.
• Sunday Champagne Brunch, 12pm to 3.30pm, on 18 and 25 October: S$258++ with Barons de Rothschild Champagne, S$698++ with Dom Pérignon 2015, or S$998++ with Cristal 2015 and 30g of Oscietra caviar. Children aged six to 12 pay S$129++, and those aged three to five pay S$64.50++.
The Ice Bar adds snow crab and oysters at Japan Week dinners from S$130++. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
The Sunday brunch is the headline
The brunch has the longest Japan Week menu. A whole hon maguro, or bluefin tuna, is carved live, and The Ice Bar has king crab, lobster claw, langoustine and yabby next to the oysters, with amaebi and tsubugai among the sashimi. Ankimo and soft shell crab rolls, unagi don with ikura and chirashi don sit next to the sushi.
The hot line has Boston lobster with uni sauce, misoyaki black cod and Hokkaido scallop with sake beurre blanc. An à la minute chef’s table cooks foie gras with smoked eel and a crystal fin chawanmushi topped with Oscietra caviar and uni foam.
At S$258++, the cheapest brunch tier is S$128 more than a Sunday-to-Thursday Japan Week dinner. The difference buys the live tuna carving, the luxury seafood and free-flow Champagne, wine, cocktails and beer.
The Japan Week Sunday brunches on 18 and 25 October start at S$258++. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
Booking and details
Seats for the two brunches are limited. All prices are before service charge and GST, and the menus are subject to change. The Japan Week menus include pork dishes.
Colony is at 7 Raffles Avenue, inside The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, a short walk from Promenade MRT station. Reservations are by phone on 6434 5288 or by email to rc.sinrz.restaurantreservations@ritzcarlton.com. Japan Week ends after dinner on 25 October.

Japan Week at Colony, The Ritz-Carlton Singapore – limited-time izakaya buffet you shouldn’t miss

members.body:
If you’re craving an all-you-can-eat Japanese feast, you’re in luck! From 16 to 25 Oct , Colony at The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore — is transforming its iconic buffet spread into a vibrant Japanese izakaya experience for Japan Week.
S howcased across Colony’s signature 7 ‘live’ conservatory kitchens where master chefs craft artisanal delights right before your eyes, this feast brings the authentic flavours of Japan to the heart of Marina Bay .
Alongside familiar offerings, Japan Week brings fresh, indulgent Japanese dishes that aren’t otherwise available at Colony. Foodies can look forward to highlights including Daily Market Fish Sashimi alongside made-to-order Salmon Crab Hand Rolls that are rolled on the spot at a dedicated Maki Station. Remember to catch the chefs in action at the 7 ‘live’ conservatory kitchens, where they masterfully whip up fresh dishes to order.
Over at the hot food section, treat yourself to a rich and savoury Salmon Mentaiyaki , comforting Unagi Omurice , and piping-hot Shrimp Tonkotsu Ramen . If you prefer classic street food with a luxurious spin, check out the Assorted Seafood Okonomiyaki with Truffle .
The best part of all is that you don’t have to choose between the all-new Japanese fare or signature local dishes. This special izakaya feature runs right alongside Colony’s usual buffet offerings, meaning you can still load up your plate with local favourites including the famous Colony Laksa , Chicken Satay , or Crackling Pork Belly .
Whether you’re celebrating a milestone occasion or simply treating yourself to an indulgent weekend treat, reserving a table ahead of time is highly recommended for this limited, 10-day showcase.
To see their full pricing tiers and operating hours, check out their official website for more information.

members.title: Japan Week at Colony, The Ritz-Carlton Singapore – limited-time izakaya buffet you shouldn’t miss

members.body:
Colony, the buffet restaurant at The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, has turned its seven kitchens over to a Japan Week menu until Sunday 25 October, with prices from S$108++ for weekday lunch to S$998++ for a Sunday brunch poured with Cristal. The Japan Week started on 16 October and covers every lunch, dinner and brunch session in the 10 days.
Japan Week runs at Colony from 16 to 25 October 2026. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
The menus mix izakaya-style Japanese dishes into Colony’s usual international and local spread rather than replacing it. The Ice Bar, The Grill and Rotisserie, The Steam Basket, The Wok, The Tandoor, The Fruit Stall and The Patisserie all stay open, and the local roast meats and wok dishes are still on the line.
Four price points, four menus
Each session has its own Japan Week menu, and the price climbs with the seafood.
• Lunch, Monday to Saturday, 12pm to 2.30pm: S$108++ an adult, S$54++ for children aged six to 12. Sashimi, nigiri, a truffle tuna roll and chilled buckwheat noodles, plus kimchi pork fried rice and pork belly yaki udon from The Wok.
• Dinner, Sunday to Thursday, 6pm to 10.30pm: S$130++ an adult, S$65++ a child. Adds freshly shucked oysters, snow crab, a negitoro avocado bruschetta, chashu omurice, menchi katsu and tori karaage with nanban sauce.
• Seafood dinner, Friday and Saturday, 6pm to 10.30pm: S$152++ an adult, or S$250++ with free-flow Barons de Rothschild Ritz Réserve Brut NV Champagne; S$76++ a child. Adds langoustine, kaki furai fried oysters, unagi omurice, a truffle seafood okonomiyaki and Singapore chilli crab with golden mantou.
• Sunday Champagne Brunch, 12pm to 3.30pm, on 18 and 25 October: S$258++ with Barons de Rothschild Champagne, S$698++ with Dom Pérignon 2015, or S$998++ with Cristal 2015 and 30g of Oscietra caviar. Children aged six to 12 pay S$129++, and those aged three to five pay S$64.50++.
The Ice Bar adds snow crab and oysters at Japan Week dinners from S$130++. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
The Sunday brunch is the headline
The brunch has the longest Japan Week menu. A whole hon maguro, or bluefin tuna, is carved live, and The Ice Bar has king crab, lobster claw, langoustine and yabby next to the oysters, with amaebi and tsubugai among the sashimi. Ankimo and soft shell crab rolls, unagi don with ikura and chirashi don sit next to the sushi.
The hot line has Boston lobster with uni sauce, misoyaki black cod and Hokkaido scallop with sake beurre blanc. An à la minute chef’s table cooks foie gras with smoked eel and a crystal fin chawanmushi topped with Oscietra caviar and uni foam.
At S$258++, the cheapest brunch tier is S$128 more than a Sunday-to-Thursday Japan Week dinner. The difference buys the live tuna carving, the luxury seafood and free-flow Champagne, wine, cocktails and beer.
The Japan Week Sunday brunches on 18 and 25 October start at S$258++. Photo: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore
Booking and details
Seats for the two brunches are limited. All prices are before service charge and GST, and the menus are subject to change. The Japan Week menus include pork dishes.
Colony is at 7 Raffles Avenue, inside The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, a short walk from Promenade MRT station. Reservations are by phone on 6434 5288 or by email to rc.sinrz.restaurantreservations@ritzcarlton.com. Japan Week ends after dinner on 25 October.

Three hotels have opened Christmas 2026 takeaway orders with early-bird cuts of 20 to 30 per cent. A whole roast turkey is listed at S$188 at Crowne Plaza Changi Airport, S$178 at Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium and S$188 before GST at Grand Copthorne Waterfront . Holiday Inn’s discount runs longest, to 9 December, while Grand Copthorne’s ends on 30 November.
The rule for this list is simple: a hotel takeaway menu that is open for orders now, with a whole-turkey price and an early-bird discount on the hotel’s own pages. The Capitol Kempinski opens on Monday and has no prices out yet, so it sits at the end.
Photo: Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel Singapore
Hotel Turkey Listed price Early bird
Crowne Plaza Changi Airport (Allora) Traditional Roast Turkey, weight not stated S$188, tax included 30 per cent online
Grand Copthorne Waterfront Roasted Turkey, 6kg, 10 to 12 people S$188 before GST 20 per cent to 30 November
Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium Traditional Roasted Turkey with Stuffing, 4kg S$178 20 per cent to 9 December
Grand Copthorne Waterfront
The 6kg Roasted Turkey is S$188 before GST and comes with giblet gravy, citrus cranberry sauce and chestnut stuffing. Food Capital’s Ginseng and Gochujang Lacquered Turkey, with glutinous rice and chestnut stuffing, is S$268 for the same 6kg. A bone-in Bourbon Pineapple Glazed Gammon Ham is also S$268, and a 1.5kg Australian grain-fed ribeye is S$228.
The early bird is 20 per cent off orders placed by 30 November, then 10 per cent off orders placed by 18 December.
Orders need three days’ notice with a 3pm daily cut-off, and full prepayment. Collection runs from 18 November to 31 December at the Level 1 festive counter, 11am to 8pm, and the last order date is 22 December. The hotel is at 392 Havelock Road, a short walk from Havelock MRT.
Crowne Plaza Changi Airport (Allora)
Allora’s Italian takeaway menu has the steepest early bird: 30 per cent off when ordered through the hotel’s online shop. The Traditional Roast Turkey is S$188 with tax included and comes brined, with chestnut stuffing, cranberry sauce and giblet gravy. The hotel does not publish the bird’s weight.
Photo: Crowne Plaza Changi Airport
Allora also sells bundles. Natale in Tavola is S$198 for a turkey and a choice of log cake and serves eight to 10. Festa di Natale pairs the Rum Honey Glazed Gammon Ham with Parmesan-crusted salmon and a log cake for S$268, and Grande Festa adds a cheese and charcuterie platter and the S$208 bone-in Brasato di Manzo short ribs for S$398. Log cakes run from S$88 to S$118.
Orders open from 6 October to 29 December, with three days’ notice. Collection is at the hotel at Changi Airport Terminal 3.
Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium
The 4kg Traditional Roasted Turkey with Stuffing and the new 4kg Japanese Miso Roasted Turkey, which comes with garlic fried rice and pickled radish, are both S$178 on the hotel’s e-store. Both carry 20 per cent off before 9 December.
Photo: Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium
Bundles start at S$318 nett before discount for the Christmas Miso Bundle, which carries a turkey, gammon, log cake, vegetables and a bottle of wine. A 3kg Honey Glazed Gammon Ham is S$168, and log cakes are S$98.
Pre-orders run to 26 December with three days’ notice, and collection is from 1 December to 2 January 2027 at the hotel at 317 Outram Road. Delivery is S$50 nett a location and free above S$400 nett. Holiday Inn’s festive menu is not halal-certified.
The Capitol Kempinski, from 19 October
Kempinski’s festive boutique opens pre-orders on Monday 19 October, with 25 per cent off festive takeaways (hampers excluded) until 30 November, then 20 per cent off from 1 to 23 December. Thanksgiving roasts get 30 per cent off for orders placed from 11 to 18 November. Collection starts on 21 November.

Calling all fashion girlies — GENTLEWOMAN and LSOUL have made their debut in Singapore with their respective stores at 313@somerset on Orchard Road . You can find GENTLEWOMAN at #03-18/21 while LSOUL is located at #03-16/17 .
Credit – gentlewomanstore.sg via Instagram
GENTLEWOMAN is a Thai fashion label best known for its iconic canvas bags featuring bold typography of its brand name. Shop them in person at their Singapore store! While you’re there, explore their other bag collections alongside their signature canvas styles.
My personal favourite is the Jelly Rush collection with jelly bags that evoke a nostalgic Y2K (2000s) feeling. Plus, these jelly bags come in trendy prints and colours like polka dot and mint green.
Credit – gentlewomanstore.sg via Instagram
If you have more bags than you can ever hold in your lifetime, browse their range of clothing collections instead. A star collection you can find here is Dormitory Darlings , a collaboration with Thai actress and model Chompoo Araya . This collection features bows and coquette-style clothing, perfect for the demure girls, or should I say, gentle women.
Other collections include Echoes Of Refinement, which explores modern elegance through clean, sharp tailoring, and Theory Of The Wind, featuring fluid silhouettes and lightweight fabrics great for Singapore’s weather.
313 Orchard Road, 313@somerset, #03-18/21, Singapore 238895
+65 6257 7679
Daily: 11am – 9.30pm
Facebook | Instagram | Website
Credit – lsoul.sg via Instagram
Located a stone’s throw away is LSOUL , a Vietnamese brand known for contemporary womenswear. Their designs are sultry and bold, with corsetry, lace detailing, and sculptural silhouettes best for statement night-out pieces.
Credit – lsoul.sg via Instagram
If you’re wondering why the clothes and shoes look so familiar, it’s because this is a brand worn by many celebrities. Stars who have donned their designs include BLACKPINK , IU , Madison Beer , and aespa — the list goes on.
313 Orchard Road, 313@somerset, #03-16/17, Singapore 238895
+65 6257 7307
Daily: 11am – 9.30pm

deals.body:
Have you passed by Spicy Hubby at Centrepoint Food Street and realised that the stall’s name rings a bell? That’s because it belongs to the same founder who owns Spicy Wife , a popular Malaysian-style nasi lemak stall at Amoy Street Food Centre that attracts long snaking queues during lunchtime.
Boasting a retro charm, the 60-seater eatery evokes the nostalgic vibe of Heap Seng Leong Coffeeshop with its signature blue-and-white tiled walls. Besides its faux retro-style windows, the space even displays old-fashioned toys and snacks for sale, just like those mama stalls that I frequented when I was still in primary school. Everything is self-service here, from placing your order at the kiosk to collecting your food.
What to order at Spicy Hubby
We started off with one of their new additions — the Nasi Ayam Gepuk (S$12.90) . A bed of nasi lemak was crowned with a whole battered chicken thigh that’s drizzled with kicap manis , served with a sunny-side-up, peanut gravy and sambal .
Just look at how glorious that chicken thigh was! Ginormous and coated in a golden-brown batter that didn’t look overly greasy, the chicken definitely made a great first impression. Unfortunately, the meat itself was devoid of any seasoning. It was only when enjoyed with the skin that the faint, sweet notes of the kicap manis truly came through.
However, pairing the chicken with the peanut sauce and s ambal combo was a game-changer in the best way possible. The peanut sauce that reminded me of the thick renditions served at hotpot places was rich and nutty, while the shiok , fiery sambal came in hot and ready to rumble. Try them together for yourself — you’ll get exactly what I mean! The rice was equally well executed, with fluffy grains and a robust coconut fragrance that tied everything nicely.
Next on our agenda was the other new kid on the block — the Nasi Rendang Ayam (S$12.90) . Sitting alongside the nasi lemak was a generous portion of chicken rendang pieces sprinkled with desicated coconut, accompanied by prawn keropok and a fried egg.
The rendang doesn’t taste like the usual ones that I have at nasi padang spots. It was saucy and undeniably unique, in a good way, with an interesting enough flavour that kept me going back for more. Those who don’t particularly enjoy fried food in general might prefer this more.
Of course, we had to get the signature Nasi Goreng Ayam Berempah (S$9.90) , a dish that made them popular at their flagship CBD hawker stall. This nasi lemak combo with a whole slab of spiced fried chicken was slightly more traditional than the other two. It came with the usual ikan bilis -peanut combo, fried egg, and sambal .
My dining partners had visited Spicy Wife before, but this was my first time trying it. Compared to the earlier Nasi Ayam Gepuk , this rendition boasted a far superior marinade. The flesh was well-seasoned, while the crispy skin was infused with an aromatic array of spices that added a ton of flavour without overwhelming the palate. The few pieces of fried curry leaves also gave an extra boost of fragrance to the chicken.
The sambal might’ve looked intimidating by its colour, but it’s actually mild with a slight hint of sweetness.
We also tried a number of their sides. The XL Otak (S$4.90) , Long Bean Sambal (S$4.90) , and Curry Fish Ball (S$6.90) .
My favourite was the Curry Fish Ball , which had a flavoursome curry and QQ fishballs. It may not look like much, but give me anything with curry and I’ll polish everything off. It tasted like the ones I had on my last Hong Kong trip. As for the XL Otak , it fell a little flat in the flavour department. If only the fish paste and spices were a tad stronger; it would’ve been much better.
Looking for a sweet little deal? Here’s one for you — from 16 to 18 Oct 2026 , Spicy Hubby is having a 1-for-1 Promotion on their 3 mains that I had just mentioned.
Who Spicy Hubby is best for
It’s perfect for non-traditionalists who have a craving for Malaysian-style nasi lemak and want to pair it with unique protein options.
How to get there?
You can take the MRT, alight at Somerset MRT Station (NS23) and head towards Centrepoint Food Street. It can get a little confusing, so go to the basement of Centrepoint, and look out for the escalator that will lead u to the Food Street. Alternatively, there are bus services bringing you to the nearest bus stops: Orchard Plaza and Opp Somerset Stn .
Do we recommend Spicy Hubby?
If you’re in the area, then Spicy Hubby is definitely worth checking out. However, with a few hits and misses, I wouldn’t specially travel all the way there just to savour a plate of Malaysian-style nasi lemak .

My favourite was the Curry Fish Ball , which had a flavoursome curry and QQ fishballs. It may not look like much, but give me anything with curry and I’ll polish everything off. It tasted like the ones I had on my last Hong Kong trip. As for the XL Otak , it fell a little flat in the flavour department. If only the fish paste and spices were a tad stronger; it would’ve been much better.
Looking for a sweet little deal? Here’s one for you — from 16 to 18 Oct 2026 , Spicy Hubby is having a 1-for-1 Promotion on their 3 mains that I had just mentioned.
Who Spicy Hubby is best for
It’s perfect for non-traditionalists who have a craving for Malaysian-style nasi lemak and want to pair it with unique protein options.
How to get there?
You can take the MRT, alight at Somerset MRT Station (NS23) and head towards Centrepoint Food Street. It can get a little confusing, so go to the basement of Centrepoint, and look out for the escalator that will lead u to the Food Street. Alternatively, there are bus services bringing you to the nearest bus stops: Orchard Plaza and Opp Somerset Stn .
Do we recommend Spicy Hubby?
If you’re in the area, then Spicy Hubby is definitely worth checking out. However, with a few hits and misses, I wouldn’t specially travel all the way there just to savour a plate of Malaysian-style nasi lemak .

The Somerset eatery also offers sides such as curry fish balls, though the mains have varying strengths and weaknesses. It is best suited for diners in the Orchard area seeking a different take on nasi lemak, rather than a destination worth travelling for specifically.

Chef Johanne Siy’s debut restaurant, Árō, prices its Chef’s Tasting Menu at S$268++ a head at 15 Mohamed Sultan Road, while over at The Singapore EDITION on Cuscaden Road, Tanica charges S$48++ for a three-course weekday lunch. Árō ‘s cooking is Creator’s Cuisine, built on lesser-known ingredients from across Asia-Pacific. Tanica cooks Southeast Asian food over a Josper grill and in the wok, meant for sharing.
Photo: Árō
The two sit at opposite ends of a night out near Orchard and River Valley, one a counter-led tasting room and the other a hotel dining room open from breakfast. Further out on Dempsey Hill, Petra opens its Mediterranean dining room on 24 October .
Árō on Mohamed Sultan Road
The name joins two words: arō, Latin for “to plough”, and áro, “love” in the dialect of the chef’s hometown. The room is small, with a counter for 10, two tables of four and a private dining room holding four tables of two. Keiji Ashizawa Design worked it in walnut, rattan, stone and bronze, and the art on the walls comes from Siy’s own collection.
Photo: Árō
For now there is one menu, the Chef’s Tasting Menu at S$268++. A shorter tasting menu is marked as coming soon, without a price yet.
Árō opens Thursday to Monday, with lunch from 12pm to 3pm and dinner from 6pm to 10pm, and closes on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Bookings go through SevenRooms, and the restaurant also takes enquiries at info@arosingapore.com.
Tanica at The Singapore EDITION
Tanica is the EDITION’s all-day restaurant at 38 Cuscaden Road, organised around herbs, spices and fire. Breakfast runs from 6.30am to 10.30am and lunch from 12pm to 2.30pm. Dinner is 6pm to 10pm from Monday to Thursday, and to 10.30pm from Friday to Sunday.
Photo: Tanica
The weekday set lunch, Monday to Friday, is three courses for S$48++ with coffee or tea, served within 60 minutes. Booking through SevenRooms comes with three hours of complimentary parking. A wagyu hanger steak main adds S$10, a glass of wine S$15 and a Saicho osmanthus sparkling tea S$12.
On Sundays the restaurant runs Sunday Table at S$98 a person, S$168 with wines, or S$198 with Louis Roederer Collection 246 champagne.
What the Tanica menu costs
The à la carte menu leans on hawker classics reworked for the grill and wok. Hokkaido sea urchin pie tee is S$30. Char kway teow, Singapore laksa noodles and Hainanese chicken rice are S$28 each. The char kway teow contains pork, and other dishes on the menu do too.
Photo: Tanica
The larger plates climb quickly. An asam pedas seafood risotto and Iga Bakar Kicap, a 72-hour wagyu short rib, are S$58 each. A one-kilogram grilled grouper is S$138, the XO mapo tofu with lobster S$128, and a 500g rib eye S$178.
Prices at both restaurants carry a 10 per cent service charge and GST.
Tanica takes reservations on +65 6329 5000 as well as SevenRooms.

Apam balik filled with Biscoff, Milo Dinosaur or even pistachio kunafa ? Singapore’s Munchi Pancakes is giving the familiar snack a rather interesting spin, and it’s opening first outlet in Malaysia this October . The halal-certified brand will make its way to AEON Mall Tebrau City , JB, bringing over 20 flavours to Malaysia after growing to more than 42 outlets across Singapore.
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
The story began in 2016, when childhood friends Calvyn and Au decided to turn their shared love for Min Jiang Kueh , also known as apam balik , into a business. Starting with a hawker stall in Yishun, the pair began experimenting with different fillings and pancake skins, giving the traditional snack a fresh spin.
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
Of course, the classics haven’t gone anywhere. Peanut , Coconut , Red Bean , Kaya and Black Sesame are still on the menu, alongside sweeter picks such as Belgian Chocolate , Milo Dinosaur , Biscoff and Oreo Cheese . For tea lovers, there’s also Matcha , Thai Milk Tea and Earl Grey to try.
Feeling a little more adventurous? Pistachio Kunafa , Kopi Gao and Pineapple Cheese offer unexpected twists on the usual fillings. Even the pancake skins get a change-up, making this more than just your standard apam balik run.
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
If you prefer your snacks in smaller portions, Mini Munchi comes in boxes of 6 , perfect for sharing or sampling a few flavours. Traditional Min Jiang Kueh is also available for those who prefer to keep things classic.
They offer vegan options, too. With old-school favourites sitting alongside more unconventional combinations, Munchi Pancakes’ JB debut gives apam balik fans in Malaysia plenty to explore. The big question is, what flavours are you looking forward to the most?

Briyani is one of the most satisfying dishes around, so why not have as much as you like? Indian Saaga on Race Course Road is offering unlimited briyani for S$38++ for two, which works out to S$19++ per person. Now that’s a steal! This deal is only available from 12pm – 6pm (Mon to Sat).
Credit – Google
Located at 38 Race Course Road, Indian Saaga is a halal-certified North Indian restaurant serving tried-and-true classics. It prides itself on affordable prices, so this deal comes as no surprise.
Some of you might recognise Indian Saaga, as it shares founders with The Song of India. That restaurant became Singapore’s first Indian restaurant to receive a Michelin star in 2016. Indian Saaga focuses on a family vibe, with big tables and plenty of seats for larger groups.
This deal, however, breaks that convention, as it is intended for pairs. So if you have a special someone, or just a buddy you want to hang out with, this deal is perfect for you.
Credit – Indian Saaga via Instagram
The deal includes 90 minutes of unlimited briyani , with a choice of chicken or mutton. Diners also get unlimited mutton curry, papad and raita , plus a 1-time serving of plain, butter or garlic naan .
Credit – Indian Saaga via Instagram
Briyani aside, the menu also has kebabs , curries and fresh naans .
Some of their popular dishes are the Mutton dum biryani (S$18++) , Chicken tikka masala (S$16++) and Goan fish curry (S$16++) . So, if you happen to feel peckish for something else, peruse the menu and maybe try something new.
Indian Saaga is open daily from 12pm – 11pm, and reservations can be made online at indiansaaga.com or via WhatsApp
at +65 9789 9004.
This deal is available for a limited time only, from 12pm – 6pm (Mon to Sat) . Head down to Indian Saaga for a hearty briyani meal.
Singapore’s highest-rated biryani has 4.9 stars — is it really that good?

Osteria Da Su opens at 163 Telok Ayer Street on Friday 23 October 2026, with 25 sharing plates from S$14++ that fold Korean accents into classic Italian cooking. The casual osteria is the newest restaurant from NAE:UM Group , next door to its one-Michelin-starred Korean fine-dining sibling NAE:UM, and is run by Korea-born Chef Suji Park.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
Opening week is dinner only. From 16 November the kitchen plans Monday to Saturday lunch and dinner. Bookings go through the restaurant’s reservation link at bit.ly/dasu.
Who is cooking
Park has cooked Italian food for close to 20 years, including stints in Bergamo, Milan and Sicily, three years at three-Michelin-starred Da Vittorio in Bergamo, two years at Claudio Sadler’s Milan trattoria, and time on the opening team of Massimo Bottura’s Gucci Osteria in Seoul. She and NAE:UM chef founder Louis Han met as students at Korea Tourism College and have been friends for 16 years. The Telok Ayer unit next to NAE:UM came up for lease in June 2026, and they opened the Italian room together.
The name works in two languages. In Italian, “da Su” reads as an osteria from Su. In Korean, “da su” means many people, which is how the kitchen frames a neighbourhood table rather than a tasting counter.
What is on the menu
Handmade pasta sits at the centre of the list. Spaghetti alle vongole is S$28++, built on asari clam stock with Korean water parsley (minari) in place of Italian parsley, and the shells removed before service. Tortelli di galbi jjim is S$30++, with Korean braised pork inside handmade tortelli and sage butter. Farfalle all’amatriciana is S$24++, finished with guanciale chips brushed in gochujang bulgogi sauce.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
Smaller plates start lower. Korean pepper fritto, a fried gochu chilli stuffed with prawn and ricotta and served with doenjang mayonnaise and balsamic soy, is S$14++. Zucchini bruschetta is S$12++, and insalata condiglione with a Korean soy-marinated egg is S$18++. For dessert, dalgona tiramisu is S$14++, a classic mascarpone and savoiardi tiramisu topped with housemade dalgona honeycomb, and salame di cioccolato is S$10++.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
The room
The restaurant seats 34: eight at the kitchen counter, 16 on banquettes and ten in a raised lounge. The fit-out mixes arched openings, terracotta floors and warm wood with a cleaner Korean line, and framed photographs Park took in Italy hang on the walls. Diners walk past the open kitchen on the way in.
Telok Ayer Street is a short walk from Telok Ayer and Downtown MRT stations. The group’s other sibling restaurant is GU:UM, a modern Korean steakhouse, which makes the Italian room its first non-Korean concept in Singapore. Prices carry a 10 per cent service charge and GST. The restaurant is not halal-certified.

Food prices are the highest they’ve ever been. Even a simple lunch in Singapore suffers from wildly high prices. Which is why I was surprised to see Mexican-inspired dishes , famous for their expensive price tag, only cost S$4.90 a piece at The Daily Fiesta in Bedok . And it’s Halal-certified as well.
But are they actually good? I went down to their second outlet to have a taste myself. I’d like to think I make pretty awesome tacos and quesadillas , so I think I’m qualified for the task ahead.
What to order at The Daily Fiesta
With the prices being so affordable, I decided to try a few of their staples. I ordered the Cajun Chicken Taco (S$4.90) , Crispy Fish Taco (S$4.90) , Chicken Quesadilla (S$13) and Beef Quesadilla (S$14) . All of them include a side of salsa and guacamole.
Let’s start with the Cajun chicken taco (S$4.90) . This one was quite a letdown compared to the other dishes. Firstly, the slaw. I found it too sweet, and it overpowered a lot of the other ingredients, namely the chicken. On top of that, they also added corn, which only made it sweeter. I would suggest replacing the slaw with regular iceberg lettuce for a more balanced flavour.
I also felt the quail egg on top was a little unnecessary, but that’s just me.
The Crispy Fish Taco (S$4.90) was much better. It had a beautifully crispy battered fish laid on top of their slaw. On top of that was a creamy sauce with a bit of spice, black ebiko and fried shallots. The flavours were a medley of sweet, salty and tart, all working in harmony. The black ebiko also added a nice popping texture when I bit into it. All in all, one of the better fish tacos I’ve had in recent memory.
Lavi Tacos: Hidden Mexican gem at Chinatown with rare birria tacos & delicious taco platters
Now, let’s move on to the quesadillas.
The Chicken Quesadilla (S$13) was pretty solid. They seared a cheese crust within the tortilla, giving an intense grilled cheese flavour. The Cajun chicken flavour was more prominent here, but I felt it still lacked intensity. As a whole, though, it was still very yummy, especially when dipped in their salsa . I would recommend increasing the spices for the Cajun chicken or marinating it for longer. Also, while the salsa was tangy with a refreshing tomato flavour, the guacamole was a bit on the sour side. It could use a bit of salt to bring out the avocado flavour.
Now this is a quesadilla! The Beef Quesadilla (S$14) was everything I wanted it to be and more. It still had the same formula: a cheese crust inside the tortilla, stringy and soft cheese, and a protein. However, the meat? Ay dios mio , it was perfectly seasoned. It had smoky, slightly spicy and rich flavours when melted together with the cheese. The meat had a bite to it, not too soft, which was my original worry.
It had to have a high fat content as well, as there was so much grease at the bottom. This is a telltale sign of a good quesadilla. Even the tortilla seems darker than the chicken version. I suspect the grease really absorbed into the tortilla, making the beef flavour very prominent in every bite.
Who is The Daily Fiesta best for?
Honestly, anyone who likes a decent Mexican lunch. I struggle to find someone who doesn’t fit in this category. Even vegetarians have options, as they have a mushroom quesadilla and taco. On top of that, they also have a variety of pastas, sides like corn ribs and much more. If you’re looking for a delicious lunch, you can’t go wrong with The Daily Fiesta.
How to get to The Daily Fiesta
Luckily for all of us, their Bedok outlet is near Bedok Mall. There is also a bus stop a few metres away called After Heartbeat @ Bedok , with several buses leading there. Alternatively, you can take the MRT to Bedok. The Daily Fiesta is only an 8-minute walk from the MRT station.
Do we recommend The Daily Fiesta?
Good food and better prices. It’s going to be hard for me not to recommend this spot. The amount of options alone makes this place worth a visit. But if I had to point to one specific dish, it has to be their Beef Quesadilla (S$14) . It really is a level above the rest, though I’m sure you will find your own favourites when you get there.
Do note that they sell out fast . I arrived an hour after opening, and their Beef Bolo Tacos were already sold out and I just managed to get their beef quesadilla , so clearly the beef is a fan favourite.

Matsuya is bringing affordable gyudon bowls to Singapore
Image credit: Japan Journeys
Joining the growing list of Japanese food chains making their way to Singapore is Matsuya , one of Japan’s most popular gyudon chains. The fast food chain has a whopping 1200 locations across Japan and has been expanding internationally since 2018. Currently, they have over 1,500 outlets globally!
Image credit: u/kccz123 via Reddit
With its first Singapore outlet opening at Suntec City in November 2026 , the brand is set to give established names such as Sukiya and Yoshinoya a run for their money.
Suntec City Food Guide: 25 Places For Cheap Kimbap, Matcha Parfait And More
While not much is known about the Singapore outlet, Matsuya is famous in Japan for its affordable gyudon bowls. A full meal there is reported to cost between ¥400 and ¥1000 , which converts to about S$3.25 to S$8.10 .
The current exchange rate is ¥ 1 = ~S$0.0081 as of 19 October 2026.
Image credit: Japan Journeys
Some popular dishes from the Japan outlets are, of course, the classic Beef Bowl (¥480) , stewed with onions in a sweet soy sauce, Beef Bowl with Tomato and Cheese (¥710), Beef Bowl topped with Grated Radish and Ponzu Citrus Soy Sauce (¥580) and more.
Image credit: Toru via Google Maps
Matsuya also offers curry bowls, including Beef Curry and Rice (¥680), Beef Curry with Cheese (¥880), and Beef Curry with Hamburg Steak (¥950) for something heartier.
Similar to many restaurants here, Matsuya uses a kiosk system that allows customers to order and pay easily.
For more delicious Japanese fare, check out these best Japanese cafes in Singapore . And we can’t mention Japan without bringing up matcha; here’s a list of the best matcha cafes according to us!
Address: 3 Temasek Boulevard, #B1-125 (Tower 2), Singapore 038983
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Matsuya is not halal-certified

Rawr Cafe is a new tiger-themed cafe in Jalan Besar
Wunderfolks , the mastermind behind Oh Wunder Cafe and Cafe Barco , is back with another concept. Its latest venture, Rawr Cafe , opened in Jalan Besar on 17 October 2027 . Unlike the other two concepts, this new cafe offers locally inspired brunch fare in a cute tiger-themed setup.
The cafe interior features adorable red-and-white tiger graphics.
You’ll also find a display of merchandise, from their house-made kaya to a tiger-inspired cap and stickers.
The menu features local flavours in the form of Western brunch classics. Some must-tries recommended by the cafe are the Singaporean Breakfast Latte ($8++) , Nasi Lemak Chicken Burger ($18++), Laksa Cream Halibut ($24++), Gula Melaka Pandan Cloud ($8++), Tiger Bomb ($12++), and Soft Shell Crab Chilli Pasta ($23++).
The Soft Shell Crab Chilli Pasta was served with a whole crab. The tomato-based sauce was sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy. Personally, it tasted more like regular red pasta sauce than chilli crab.
The soft-shell crab appeared to be lightly battered and deep-fried, giving it a crispy exterior. Beneath the shell was tender, fleshy crab meat with some creamy roe. The crab had some natural sweetness and brininess that came through nicely.
The Nasi Lemak Chicken Burger was extremely hearty, layered with fried chicken, fresh lettuce, and cucumber, then topped with ikan bilis and sambal for that bold umami flavour.
For sides, we got the Prawn Paste Chicken ($15++) . It tasted like regular har cheong gai—the exterior was fried till crisp, coating the greasy, tender chicken wing. I noticed that the chicken meat was a little pinker than what I was used to, so I thought it could’ve been cooked for longer.
We also got two of the signature drinks: the SG Breakfast Latte, a creamy pandan latte, and Tiger Bomb, espresso topped with orange foam.
Image credit: Rawr Cafe
You can also choose to top your drinks with an adorable Raw Tiger Cookie Topper for just $2++!
The SG Breakfast Latte caught our eye with its e foamy “fried egg” on top. It’s served with a crunchy slab of kaya toast, which was light, fragrant, and perfect for soaking up the latte. FYI: the “yolk” in the foam is kaya-flavoured!
The Tiger Bomb had an intense citrusy flavour, thanks to the addition of the orange-infused foam. Paired with espresso, it made for a unique flavour combination that’s worth trying.
Overall, Rawr Cafe is definitely worth a visit if you love cutesy cafes. The SG Breakfast Latte is my favourite in terms of taste and appearance, so give it a go!
Cafe-hoppers, here are some new restaurants and cafes that opened in October 2026 ! And for more authentic local eateries, here is the ultimate Singapore food guide .
Address: 134 Jalan Besar, Singapore 208852
Opening hours: Daily 9:30am to 9pm
Website
Rawr Cafe is not halal-certified.

Overall, Rawr Cafe is definitely worth a visit if you love cutesy cafes. The SG Breakfast Latte is my favourite in terms of taste and appearance, so give it a go!

Huaiyang set lunches start at S$98++ a person at Imperial Treasure Moutai House , the restaurant Imperial Treasure has opened for reservations inside Moutai House at The Fullerton Waterboat House.
Scallops with preserved mei cai are part of the S$98++ Lunch Course A. Photo: Imperial Treasure
The 45-seat dining room is at #03-01, 3 Fullerton Road, with nine tables, one private room and a wine cellar. It opens daily from 11am to 3pm and 6pm to 10pm. The nearest MRT station is Raffles Place.
The idea is Moutai at the dinner table, poured with the food rather than saved for a toast. Imperial Treasure cooks Huaiyang cuisine, the eastern Chinese tradition of careful knife work and slow braises, alongside the sour and spicy flavours of Guizhou, the province where Kweichow Moutai is distilled.
Five set menus, S$98++ to S$398++
Lunch Course A, at S$98++ a person, is the entry point. It opens with a Huaiyang trio of marinated pig’s head, Yangzhou-style fried cod and pickled radish skin, then shredded beancurd with uni in thick soup, braised pork meat ball with abalone, scallops sauteed with preserved mei cai, Yangzhou fried rice and a seasonal dessert.
Lunch Course B is S$138++ a person, for a minimum of two. It adds yellow-braised shark’s fin with seafood and bamboo pith, shrimp with honey peas in black truffle oil, and Jiangnan braised pork with a five-head fresh abalone.
Pork meat ball soup in Yangzhou style is on the a la carte soup list. Photo: Imperial Treasure
Dinner runs on three courses, all for two or more. Course C is S$188++ with steamed soft-shell turtle in chicken oil and braised pork with Hokkaido sea cucumber. Course D is S$328++, with shark’s fin in sour soup and eight-head Australian dried abalone. Course E, at S$398++, includes egg white sauteed with caviar and a 15-head South African dried whole abalone with superior fish maw.
The a la carte premiums
Luxury items are priced by the piece. A whole premium sea cucumber is S$500, or S$250 for half. Superior fish maw is S$66 a piece, a whole Hokkaido sea cucumber S$54 and a five-head fresh abalone S$46 each, with a choice of braised in brown sauce, deep-fried with scallion or yellow-braised.
Live fish, including coral trout, soon hock and empurau, is priced per 100g, and the empurau needs advance ordering. Every price is subject to service charge and GST. Pork runs through the menu, so the restaurant is not halal.
Design render of the restaurant entrance at #03-01, 3 Fullerton Road. Photo: Imperial Treasure
The restaurant shares The Fullerton Waterboat House, part of The Fullerton Heritage, with Moutai House’s own rooftop bar. Reservations for Imperial Treasure Moutai House are on 8666 9778.

deals.body:
Two all-day restaurants now share the Ginger Garden at Singapore Botanic Gardens, with brunch from a S$14 kaya brown loaf and soft-boiled eggs up to a S$45 ribeye off the charcoal grill. Tembusu , a Straits dining house from Fleursophy Group, runs the Ginger Garden building that was home to The Halia, while The Bloomhouse by Little Farms sits a few steps away at Block 2, with its own Picnic Basket kiosk.
The rule for this list is simple: places to eat inside the Ginger Garden with a menu their operator published for September or October 2026. Three made it. Prices at both restaurants are subject to GST and service charge.
Tembusu opens 8am to 9pm from Wednesday to Sunday. Photo: Tembusu
Tembusu
Tembusu cooks local and Straits dishes under timber beams, with tall windows onto the garden. Brunch is where the menu is most local: the homemade kaya brown loaf with French butter and two free-range soft-boiled eggs is S$14, and the Tembusu nasi lemak with blue pea basmati rice, chicken hindquarter, sambal, achar and otah is S$26.
Later in the day, udon laksa with Andaman sea prawn, surimi and sakura ebi is S$25, the Singapore chilli crab pasta with soft-shell crab and blue swimmer crab is S$27, and an Andaman prawn risotto in lobster bisque is S$32. Kopi and teh start at S$5.50, made with beans from Vietnam’s Gia Lai Highlands roasted in Singapore by Generation Coffee Roasters.
Two details matter for planning. Pets are allowed in the air-conditioned dining room, which is rare inside the Gardens. Local craft beer on tap drops to S$13 from S$16 during happy hour, noon to 5pm.
Tembusu opens 8am to 6pm on Mondays and Tuesdays, and 8am to 9pm from Wednesday to Sunday. A kids’ section has a junior chicken burger combo at S$16 and a cherry tomato pasta at S$12.
Pets are allowed in Tembusu’s air-conditioned dining room. Photo: Tembusu
The Bloomhouse by Little Farms
The Bloomhouse is open every day from 7.30am to 8pm. Its menu, updated on 1 September, works ginger and other botanicals from the ginger family into the cooking, a nod to the garden outside.
Breakfast runs until 2pm. The Bloomhouse forest omelette is S$19, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon or nitrate-free ham is S$24, and the brekkie platter with two eggs, pork sausage, bacon and sourdough is S$33.
From 11am the kitchen moves to bowls, pasta and a charcoal grill. The Bloomhouse bowl with spiced chicken, avocado and wild rice is S$22. Its chilli crab fettuccine with fried mantou is S$30, three dollars more than Tembusu’s chilli crab pasta next door. The grill has a 250g picanha at S$38 and a 300g ribeye at S$45, and the Bloomhouse burger with a 180g beef patty is S$30.
The Bloomhouse menu starts at S$19 for its forest omelette. Photo: Little Farms
Picnic Basket
Picnic Basket is The Bloomhouse’s takeaway counter, for anyone heading out onto the lawns rather than sitting down. Coffee starts at S$5.50 for an espresso, a long black or flat white is S$6.50, and house teas such as Ginger Garden herbal, with blue pea, torch ginger and lemongrass, are S$8.50.
Smoothies are S$12. Hot sandwiches run from S$11 for a ham and cheese croissant to S$14 for mortadella and scamorza. Event and group bookings go to events@littlefarms.com.
Picnic Basket is The Bloomhouse’s takeaway counter. Photo: Little Farms
Getting there
Both restaurants are inside the Ginger Garden at 1 Cluny Road, deeper in the Gardens than the Nassim Gate visitor centre that map apps point to. The nearest MRT station is Botanic Gardens on the Circle and Downtown lines; enter by the Bukit Timah Gate and walk through to the Ginger Garden. Drivers should use the Learning Forest carpark, the closest drop-off point.
Both menus include pork dishes, and neither restaurant states a halal certification. Tembusu takes general enquiries at hello@tembusu.sg.

deals.body: 2 for $22 / 2 for $33 Pizza Hut Singapore is bringing back its 2-for-$22 regular / 2-for-$33 large pizza deal from 21 October to 11 November 2026, on delivery and self-collection via its website and app only. Each pair mixes one limited-time Cheesy 7 pizza (five flavours, including Soy Garlic Chicken and Otah Laksa) with one Favourite-range pizza, against usual prices of $57.90 and $81.80. We checked Pizza Hut's own order system on 20 October: the standing 50%-off two-pizza deals sell at $28.90 and $40.80, so the comeback prices genuinely beat them. For one week (21-27 October), five outlets also sell $4.90 regular Favourite pizzas for walk-in takeaway or self-collection, two per customer, while stocks last.

Greenwood Fish Market VivoCity opens on 4 November 2026 at #01-188. Photo: Greenwood Fish Market
Greenwood Fish Market opens its first shopping mall outlet at VivoCity on 4 November 2026, 23 years after the seafood retailer and restaurant started on Greenwood Avenue in Bukit Timah. The Greenwood Fish Market VivoCity bistro sits at #01-188, next to TANGS and Tiong Bahru Bakery, and opens daily from 12pm to 10.30pm.
A bistro, not a third restaurant
VivoCity is the brand’s third address, after Bukit Timah and the Quayside Isle restaurant on Sentosa, which opened in 2015. It is also the first Greenwood Fish Market bistro. Founder David Lee told AsiaOne that half of the bistro menu carries Greenwood signatures, with the other half made up of new tapas, small plates and oshizushi, the pressed sushi. He also told AsiaOne that the outlet is a test bed for global franchising.
The bistro’s own recommendations are oysters, pastas, oshizushi and sharing plates. Alfresco seats are pet friendly, as they are at the two older outlets.
Set lunch and set dinner prices
The VivoCity set lunch runs Monday to Friday, 12pm to 5pm. Screenshot: Greenwood Fish Market, 21 October 2026
The three-course set lunch is S$29.95++ for a starter, a main and coffee or tea, from Monday to Friday, 12pm to 5pm. It does not run on public holidays or their eves. Starters include lobster bisque, assorted sashimi and hand-cut calamari. Mains include snapper fish and chips, prawn aglio, grilled barramundi and an Angus cheeseburger, while steak frites carries a S$12 supplement and pan-seared John Dory a S$10 supplement.
The four-course set dinner is S$45.95++ with a starter, a main, a dessert and a hot drink. Mains include a seafood marinara baked in a paper parcel, John Dory, steak frites and an A5 wagyu hamburg rice bowl. Black cod carries a S$14 supplement and USDA Choice ribeye a S$19 supplement.
Details
Greenwood Fish Market is not halal-certified, though the kitchen prepares dishes free of pork and alcohol when told in advance. Corkage is S$50++ for a bottle of wine and S$80++ for a bottle of spirits, and one bottle is waived for every bottle bought from the menu. VivoCity is linked to HarbourFront MRT station on the North East and Circle lines.

Orang Laut SG , the community group that has sold Southern Islander food mostly through weekend deliveries since 2020, opens its first walk-in cafe on Friday, 23 October, CNA Lifestyle reported. Called Terumbu, it runs at Chef X, #03-103/104 Clarke Quay Central, until 26 December.
Terumbu opens at Chef X on 23 October. Photo: Orang Laut SG
Terumbu is Malay for coral reefs. The pop-up is the 15th residency at Chef X, Far East Organization’s space for home-based and private-dining cooks to run a commercial restaurant for a fixed stint, with a professional kitchen, a dining room for up to 24 and mentoring from chef Isaac Tan of Commonwealth Concepts.
Two savoury dishes and island kueh
The menu is short. The Pulau Bowl is S$15.90 and puts three seafood dishes over jasmine rice with vegetables: asam pedas ikan karang (coral reef fish in a sour, spicy gravy), sotong hitam (squid cooked in its own ink) and sambal udang (stir-fried prawns in sambal).
The sotong hitam uses green-eyed squid, known as sotong nos, which is traditionally caught by line. The family picks it for the amount of ink it carries.
The second dish is bubur lambuk tenggiri, a Spanish mackerel porridge cooked with lemongrass, coconut milk and black pepper. It is S$11.90 with prawns or with squid, and S$13.90 with both.
Bubur lambuk tenggiri is S$11.90 with prawns or squid. Photo: Orang Laut SG
This is not the bubur lambuk handed out at mosques during Ramadan. On the islands it was an everyday dish, made by grinding leftover coral fish, bones and all, at a time when families had no fridge to keep the catch.
Dessert is kueh koleh-koleh and puteri salat, made by a former Pulau Bukom islander. The menu names coral fish without naming the species, because the fish changes with what islander fishermen bring in, including the few bubu (fish trap) makers who still go out to sea.
A family kitchen from Pulau Semakau
Founder Firdaus Sani is a fourth-generation Orang Pulau and Orang Laut whose family lived on Pulau Semakau for generations. They were moved to the mainland in 1977, and the island is now Singapore’s offshore landfill.
His mother does most of the cooking at Terumbu, with his aunt Rohaini running the floor and cousins helping out. The recipes come from his grandmother, Nenek Ninah, and are cooked by feel rather than by measurement.
The family runs Terumbu’s kitchen and floor. Photo: Orang Laut SG
Orang Laut SG started in 2020 as an Instagram page recording the memories, food and traditions of communities moved off the Southern Islands. Terumbu also has a small community gallery on the history of those islands.
Details
Details from CNA Lifestyle:
• Where: Chef X, #03-103/104 Clarke Quay Central, 6 Eu Tong Sen Street, above Clarke Quay MRT station
• When: 23 October to 26 December 2026
• Prices: Pulau Bowl S$15.90; bubur lambuk tenggiri S$11.90 (prawn or squid) or S$13.90 (both)

Brewed by Davine is a home-based cafe in Bukit Batok
Westies looking for an affordable matcha fix: this home-based business needs to be on your radar. Tucked away in a Bukit Batok HDB flat, Brewed by Davine is run by 20-year-old Davine, who serves freshly made matcha drinks straight from her HDB window, with occasional help from her little sister.
With matcha averaging around $7 a cup in Singapore, Davine’s $4.50 Matcha Peng is a steal. She keeps prices low using the oldest trick in the book: old-school kopi peng plastic bags. While most hawkers are transitioning to plastic cups, Brewed by Davine unintentionally keeps the tradition alive, making her matcha affordable and nostalgic.
The localised matcha is under the Peng series. Specifically, the Matcha Peng ($4.50), Milo Sea Salt Peng ($5), and Atas Teh Peng ($5) , which is matcha flavoured with Earl Grey and vanilla. There’s also a Salty Gula Melaka Kopi Peng ($6) , but that is served in a cup.
If you prefer, you can opt for all your drinks to be served in a cup for an extra $0.50.
We were lucky enough to watch her make it from scratch—she started by whisking the matcha powder with some water.
She then filled a bag with milk and poured in the matcha.
The classic Matcha Peng was milky and smooth, with earthy green tea notes that came through nicely. It also had just the right amount of sweetness, making for a well-balanced drink.
The Milo Sea Salt Peng was also milky, but it was a little sweeter and creamier due to the foam. The sea salt was a great addition, cutting through the richness so it didn’t get too jelak .
Davine also recommended her Sibei Chio ($6.50) , which is matcha layered with butterfly pea flower milk and homemade strawberry puree. Sibei Chio is one of her best-sellers. Similar to the rest, this drink was very creamy; however, the puree added a nice strawberry flavour and chunkiness from the fruit.
Her desserts are also loved among regulars, with the Biscoff Banana Shiok ($8) a crowd favourite.
The custard was thick and rich, with a distinct banana flavour. The Biscoff cookie’s cinnamon flavour complemented the banana and made for a great crunchy-on-creamy texture.
As F&B gets increasingly dominated by chain stores and corporations, make sure you also show some love to our local businesses! Don’t worry, the drinks will be well worth it.
For more home-based businesses you can support, check out these best home cafes in Singapore . If you’re considering making your own matcha, here are the best matcha powders to get you started.
Address: 161 Bukit Batok Street 11, #650161, Singapore 650161
Opening hours:Wed-Fri 12pm to 5pm, Sat-Sun 10am to 5pm
Website
Brewed by Davine is not halal-certified.

Photos taken by Marcus Neo.
This was an independent visit by Eatbook.sg.

Pizza Hut Singapore brings back $4.90 pizza deal
Good news for pizza fans: from 21 to 27 October 2026 , five Pizza Hut Singapore outlets are selling Regular Favourite pizzas for $4.90 each, down from the usual $23.95. That’s about 80% off, which makes it a steal.
The five outlets are located at Bedok North , Crown Centre , ESR Chai Chee , Waterway Sunrise , and West Coast . The deal is available all day for walk-in takeaway or self-collection via the Hut Rewards app or website, while stocks last.
14 Best Pizza In Singapore For All Budgets, Including Hawker Stalls And Famous Restaurants
Pizza Hut is also bringing back their two-pizza bundles until 11 November 2026 . Diners can snag two Regular pizzas for $22 or two Large pizzas for $33 —that works out to about $11 and $16.50 per pizza, almost up to 62% off the usual prices for each pair.
The bundles are available for delivery or self-collection via Pizza Hut’s website or app, while stocks last.
Each bundle comes with one Cheesy 7 pizza, which comprises a blend of seven cheeses. You can pick from five Cheesy 7 flavours: Soy Garlic Chicken , Original , Hawaiian , Pepperoni , and the locally inspired Otah Laksa .
The Otah Laksa pairs smoky, savoury otah with a laksa-inspired drizzle on top of the seven-cheese blend.
For the other pizza, you can go for one of six Favourites , from the veggie-friendly Cheesy Spinach and Simply Cheese to meatier picks including Very Beefy and Chic Ham ’N’ Shroom , plus BBQ Chunky Chic and Cheese ’N’ Chic .
Pizza crust options include Pan , Sourdough , Crackin’ Thin Crust , and Cheesy Stuffed Crust . Do note that additional charges apply for Classic and Specialty flavours.
In more fast food news, KFC is bringing back its Samyang Buldak Carbonara collab with a new macaroni bowl, while McDonald’s McGriddles are also back on the menu for a limited time.

Pizza Hut is not halal-certified.

Barossa Steak & Grill is an Australian-inspired steakhouse and bar that has reopened its doors at VivoCity with a refreshed menu and is celebrating this occasion with an amazing deal you don’t want to miss!
Credit: Barossa Steak & Grill
How do you like your steak done? Rare, medium, or well done? Well, the first 100 customers daily can make that decision and enjoy Australian F1 Wagyu Oyster Balde Steak for just S$12++ (U.P. S$68++) from 2 to 15 November . Be among the first to queue, as the promotion is valid for walk-ins only , with one steak order per person . Do note that the promotion does not include any sides and is served à la carte.
Some starters from the revamped menu that pair well with the steak include Burrata and Beets (S$27) , Borrasa Spin Spin Salad (S$20) , and their Home-Made Potato Chips (S$16) – all recommended and great for sharing. You can also indulge in their Lobster Bisque (S$22) or Wild Mushroom Soup (S$16) if you’d prefer something lighter!
If you’re dining from Sunday to Thursday , enjoy their Golden Hour Happy Pours from 4pm to 7pm . Sip their House Pour Wines and Prosecco for $10 or Cocktails at S$14 – Mojito, Margarita, Old Fashioned, Whiskey Highball, and Gin and Tonic. You could also enjoy a chilly pint of crispy Beer from Carlsberg or Sapporo for S$14 , from 12pm to 7pm .
Gather your friends and family, then treat yourself to Barossa’s Wagyu Steak at a price that’s hard to beat.

deals.body:
Located at Kukoh 21 Food Centre , The $2.50 Shop is a Muslim -owned stall that features over 14 dishes, with everything on the menu going for just S$2.50 each .
Run by 40-year-old Hani Isnin-Racine and her parents, both in their 70s, the trio has been operating this brand for slightly over 2 years. Prior to this, they operated another stall at the same location, offering similar dishes at higher prices.
“We started the S$2.50 meals initiative to help lessen the burden of the vulnerable community (single parents and senior folks who aren’t working due to chronic illness or disability),” Hani shared.
To be ready for their 4.30am (i’m in dreamland at this hour) opening, they arrive at 2am to begin preparations. When asked why they open so early, Hani explained, “We cater to older folks with different sleep patterns due to medication, or those needing to visit the kidney dialysis centre to ‘ chope ‘ good seats for their session.”
What I tried at The $2.50 Shop
With so many choices, I needed a good 5 minutes to decide what to get. After much deliberation, I got the ball rolling with the Nasi Rawon (S$2.50) , with an option to have it either with Cuttlefish or Paru (beef lung).
I chose the latter, and the mound of rice was topped with a generous serving of serundeng , accompanied by sambal goreng , half a bergedil , a bowl of beef stock, and sambal belacan . For its price point, the ingredients were definitely generous.
The beef stock was rich and complex, filled with a few beef chunks. Each spoonful of gravy over the rice was a burst of flavours; a rave party in my mouth.
Hani shared that her mum prepares the sambal belacan fresh daily, using small kampung chilli padi that’s thoroughly washed and deseeded. It delivered a powerful spice kick that jolted my taste buds, waking me up even before my morning coffee— hot but shiok !
I’ve tried paru at several other stalls, and it has always been the same— dry and slightly tough. Thankfully, the version here was soft and moist.
Next, we tried the Lontong (S$2.50) . The rice cake pieces were doused in a thick creamy gravy with a mixture of braised cabbage, long beans and carrots, served with spiced grated coconut and a dollop of nasi lemak sambal .
The pieces of lontong were pillowy, melting in my mouth with ease, and the veggies were braised to a perfect softness.
The gravy had mellow, sweet notes and was prepared with seniors in mind, using a 50/50 blend of pure coconut milk and low-fat milk to keep it low in cholesterol. It was lighter and didn’t feel too jelak , even after many spoonfuls.
The sambal egg was a nice touch. According to Hani’s mum, Mdm Mai, the sambal is cooked for at least 6 hours, with constant skimming of the chilli oil that’s accumulated at the top.
We still had room and gave the Mee Goreng (S$2.50) a try. The stir-fried yellow noods had bits of crab stick, cubes of tau kwa , tau geh , a piece of onion omelette, sambal , then garnished with ku chye , fried shallots and half a calamansi.
To add some brightness, I squeezed in some calamansi juice— hello burst of citrusy goodness!
After mixing the noodles with the sambal , each bite started with a fiery kick that lingered briefly before it faded, leaving only a gentle numbness on your tongue.
There was also a large slab of onion omelette in it— just look at the size! How can this plate cost only S$2.50 ?!
The stall also has a variety of handmade Kueh – Kueh (S$0.80 for 1 , S$2 for 4) . There’s goreng pisang and epok epok , too. The Kueh Kodok Pisang was a moist and fragrant banana ball of deliciousness. My only gripe? Certain parts were slightly dark, resulting in a mild bitterness.
I also tried the Ondeh Ondeh , Kueh Kosui and Kueh Sago . All of them were decent, coated with shredded coconut.
Final thoughts
By the time you’ve reached this paragraph, you’re probably wondering, “Do they actually make a profit?”
Hani was very honest and added, “No, we don’t. There are many monthly bills to settle besides rent and utilities. But despite these sacrifices, it’s worth it when we can help ease the daily lives of the elderly.”
If you’re thinking of swinging by The $2.50 Shop, be sure to check their Facebook page. Hani’s mum’s health has deteriorated since she suffered a minor fracture at work last October— wishing you a speedy recovery!
Let’s support these 3 beautiful, kind-hearted souls. I have the utmost respect for them and am honoured to have made their acquaintance.

Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee is opening in Tampines
Image credit: @ngkuanchillipanmee
Easties who are always on the hunt for late-night supper spots will soon have a new go-to. Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee is opening its fifth location at Century Square in mid-November 2026— shoppers at the mall have already spotted its hoarding next to popular Taiwanese restaurant Abundance .
Tampines 1 Food Guide: 12 Places For Warabimochi, Famous HK Teppanyaki And More
While opening hours for Ng Kuan’s new branch are yet to be announced, their other outlets are known to open late into the night or even 24 hours, making it an ideal spot for night owls. Beyond that, the store’s Malaysian-style pan mee is loved for its punchy, bold flavours.
You can get their Signature Ban Mian with soup ($6.50) or as a bowl of dry noodles for $6.80 . Each dish comes with al dente noodles, minced pork, ikan billis, fried shallots, garlic, a runny egg, and the star ingredient—hae-bee-infused chilli.
You can also choose from four types of noodles: mee sua, mee hoon kueh, you mian, and ban mian.
For a heartier option, you can add more protein with the Chicken Cutlet , Fish Cutlet , or Pork Cutlet ban mian at $8.80 each .
Alternatively, if you’re after something lighter, consider the Lala Soup ($6.80) , Spinach Soup with Noodles ($7.80) , or just a plain Spinach Soup ($6.80) .
For groups who love to share, there is also a huge selection of sides, including Boiled Lala with Garlic and Chilli ($6.80) , Spinach with Homemade Chilli Sauce ($6.80) , and even Deep-Fried Squid Tentacles ($10) .
If you’re a ban mian fan, read our list of best ban mian in Singapore for $2.50 noodles, abalone mee hoon kueh and more. While you’re in the East, check out our Tampines mall food guide , which will show you the best eats.
Address: 2 Tampines Central 5, #01-34, Century Square, Singapore 529509
Opening hours: TBD
Website
Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee is not halal-certified.
Tampines Mall Food Guide: 10 Eateries For Affordable Ramen, K-BBQ Buffet And More
Feature image adapted from Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee

deals.body: Buffets from $22.88/pax + 10% early bird Neo Group's value catering arm Deli Hub has released its Christmas Edition 2026 menus, running 2 November 2026 to 3 January 2027. The headline numbers: five festive buffets from $22.88 per guest (before GST), mini buffets in self-heating containers from $25.99, Christmas bentos from $8 a set, a Santa's High Tea at $23.80, roast bundles from $149.80 and a 10-dish Christmas Party Pack at $388 for 8 to 10 guests. The early bird is the real lobang: order by 4 December 2026 and the regular Christmas buffets are 10% off, though the cheapest Little Red Dot menu is excluded and nothing applies on 24 December. Budget for the fine print too: delivery runs $45 to $90 per location with a $420 minimum order, buffet setups add a 10% service charge, and credit cards add a 3% admin fee.
